supplemented_raw_records.title: Silent orchestra: Co-occurring deficits in mental imagery and music reward
supplemented_raw_records.abstract: Mental imagery and music reward have been traditionally studied separately. Across five experiments, we examined their connection. Experiments 1 and 2 showed a significant correlation between sensitivity to musical reward and visual imagery vividness in the general population. Experiment 3 compared aphantasics (inability to form mental images;  N  = 25) with controls ( N  = 25). 44% of the aphantasics met criteria for music anhedonia (inability to experience music reward). In experiment 4 ( N  = 19), all aphantasics with specific music anhedonia met the criteria for anauralia (inability to form auditory imagery). Lastly, we replicated the main findings of experiments 3 and 4 in a larger sample of aphantasics, further demonstrating a strong link between specific music anhedonia and anauralia (experiment 5;  N  = 42). Overall, these results demonstrate a link between mental imagery vividness and sensitivity to musical reward and suggest that auditory imagery may play a key role in the experience of musical pleasure.

supplemented_raw_records.title: Learning societies as catalysts for climate resilience: A systematic review and meta-analysis of community-based environmental education models
supplemented_raw_records.abstract: Climate change demands social responses beyond technical fixes. Community-based environmental education (CBEE) embeds climate learning within communities, aligning with the learning-society emphasis on distributed knowledge and adaptive governance. We synthesized global evidence to characterize CBEE models, quantify their associations with resilience outcomes, and examine mediators and moderators. Following PRISMA 2020, we searched six databases (2014–2024) and analyzed 127 studies (48,592 participants, 42 countries) using random-effects meta-analysis, meta-regression, and meta-analytic structural equation modeling. Three models emerged: Participatory Learning Networks, Place-Based Learning Communities, and Transformative Learning Partnerships. CBEE showed large associations with social cohesion, environmental stewardship, and adaptive capacity, exceeding traditional education, although heterogeneity was substantial. Social capital, collective efficacy, knowledge integration, institutional capacity, and adaptive learning mediated these associations, which cultural relevance and collaboration strengthened. These patterns clarify how community education can support climate resilience and inform the design of context-sensitive, equitable programs. Registration: This review was prospectively registered with PROSPERO (CRD420261411683).

supplemented_raw_records.title: Ovarian function via gut microbiota-driven serotonin dysregulation in zebrafish
supplemented_raw_records.abstract: Ciprofloxacin (CIP) is frequently detected in aquatic environments, yet its effects on reproduction through gut microbiota-mediated pathways remain unclear. Adult female zebrafish were exposed to 5,000 ng/L CIP for 30 days and evaluated using histology, hormone assays, metagenomics, metabolomics, transcriptomics, and fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT). CIP impaired folliculogenesis, reduced follicle-stimulating hormone, luteinizing hormone, and estradiol levels, and disrupted intestinal barrier integrity. Multi-omics analyses revealed gut dysbiosis and altered microbial metabolism, including increased serotonin (5-HT) and indole-3-lactic acid associated with  Cetobacterium  and  Plesiomonas shigelloides . Brain transcriptomics showed suppressed hormone signaling and elevated 5-HT, consistent with hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis disruption. FMT from CIP-exposed donors reproduced hormonal and ovarian abnormalities in microbiota-depleted recipients. This study underscores the need to integrate microbiota-host interactions into the risk assessment of emerging aquatic contaminants and highlights the broader implications of environmental exposures for reproductive and endocrine health in both aquatic organisms and potentially humans.

supplemented_raw_records.title: Geographic and thematic gaps in wildfire resilience research
supplemented_raw_records.abstract: Wildfires are becoming more frequent and destructive around the world, threatening lives, homes, and natural landscapes. Building or maintaining systems for wildfire resilience has emerged as a crucial strategy for addressing wildfire risks and impacts, balancing a need for fire on the landscape to support healthy natural systems with a desire to mitigate loss of human life and structure. Our review of over 1,500 wildfire resilience studies shows that while research is growing, it is unevenly distributed across regions and topics, often focusing on habitats while paying less attention to human communities, infrastructure, and other aspects that matter for people's lives and well-being. By highlighting these gaps, our work helps guide scientists, policymakers, and communities toward more integrated and equitable strategies for living safely with fire. Understanding where research is lacking can improve planning, strengthen resilience efforts, and support decisions that protect both people and ecosystems.

supplemented_raw_records.title: Seasonal spectral separation of shrub and herbaceous vegetation using in situ hyperspectral and Sentinel-2 data
supplemented_raw_records.abstract: Shrub encroachment is reshaping alpine grasslands on the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau and requires reliable remote sensing approaches to separate shrubs from herbaceous vegetation across seasons. We combined  in situ  Analytical Spectral Devices (ASD) hyperspectral measurements with Sentinel-2 multispectral observations to characterize canopy spectra and quantify separability during early-growing, peak-growing, and senescence stages using band sensitivity analysis, univariate separability metrics, vegetation indices, and satellite-scale evaluation. Green (505-570 nm) and near-infrared (750-900 nm) regions provided strong separation, while Sentinel-2 retained diagnostic contrast in visible (B3-B5) and near-infrared (B8) bands, with June emerging as the most favorable period. Vegetation indices showed phenology-dependent performance: Corrected Transformed Vegetation Index (CTVI) and Transformed Vegetation Index (TVI) were effective in early and late seasons, IPVI performed well at peak and senescence, and Transformed Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (TNDVI) remained stable across stages. Although Sentinel-2 was less discriminative than hyperspectral data, selected bands and indices still supported effective shrub-herbaceous separation for landscape-scale monitoring.

supplemented_raw_records.title: System level life cycle and performance assessment of a sustainable Mahua cashew shell hybrid biolubricant
supplemented_raw_records.abstract: Biolubricants derived from renewable oils can reduce dependence on petroleum, but their environmental performance also depends on oil modification, additives, and processing energy. In the present study, a fully formulated lubricant based on chemically modified mahua oil and cashew nut shell oil was evaluated through physicochemical, engine, biological, and cradle-to-gate life cycle assessments. The formulation showed lower friction and comparable wear, improved brake thermal efficiency, lower specific fuel consumption, and reduced exhaust emissions relative to commercial SAE 20W40 oil. Microbial growth screening indicated greater microbial utilization potential, while brine shrimp and L929 cell assays showed lower toxicity under the tested conditions. Life cycle assessment identified OA-hBN synthesis and blended-oil production as major environmental hotspots. Scenario analysis showed that removing OA-hBN reduced global warming impact by 60.5%, while renewable electricity produced a 5.8% reduction. These findings highlight formulation and process optimization as key pathways for improving biolubricant sustainability.

supplemented_raw_records.title: Ancient human genomes reveal farmer-pastoralist interactions in the formation of Iron Age Qin people
supplemented_raw_records.abstract: The Yellow River's Ji-shaped bend region is a key agro-pastoral transition zone in northern China, yet the genetic interactions between Central Plain farmers and Eastern Eurasian Steppe pastoralists remain unclear. We analyzed three Late Neolithic individuals from the Lushanmao site and 34 Iron Age individuals from the Liuying site associated with the Qin people. The Lushanmao population derived ∼93% of its ancestry from Yangshao-related Yellow River farmers (NYR) and ∼7% from Ancient Northeast Asian (ANA) pastoralists. The Iron Age Qin people retained dominant NYR ancestry and minor ANA ancestry while acquiring an additional southern East Asian (SEA)-related components. However, the Qin people showed no detectable West Eurasian genetic influence, indicating that West Eurasian cultural elements in Qin culture were not accompanied by genetic admixture. These findings illuminate the complex farmer-pastoralist interactions that shaped populations in this strategically important region.

supplemented_raw_records.title: Prognostic value of circulating cell-free Epstein-Barr virus DNA CpG methylation in extranodal NK/T cell lymphoma
supplemented_raw_records.abstract: Extranodal NK/T cell lymphoma (ENKTL) is an Epstein-Barr virus (EBV)-associated malignancy, and circulating EBV DNA serves as a key prognostic indicator. Because tumor-derived EBV DNA typically exhibits CpG methylation, this prospective study evaluated the prognostic role of circulating cell-free CpG-methylated EBV DNA compared with matched EBV DNA from whole blood and plasma in 43 newly diagnosed ENKTL patients. While 74.4% and 69.8% were positive for whole-blood and plasma EBV DNA at diagnosis, respectively, only 27.9% were positive for CpG-methylated EBV DNA. High CpG methylation index correlated with greater tumor burden and inferior treatment response. Notably, only CpG-methylated EBV DNA, not whole-blood or plasma EBV DNA, effectively identified high-risk patients and predicted significantly poorer outcomes ( p  < 0.001). Integrating it into the prognostic index of natural killer cell lymphoma (PINK) model created PINK-CpGE, which showed improved predictive accuracy (AUC 0.9333 vs. 0.8897). Overall, cell-free CpG-methylated EBV DNA served as a superior prognostic biomarker for ENKTL.

supplemented_raw_records.title: Embryonic stem cells do not have a globally disrupted higher-order chromatin fiber structure
supplemented_raw_records.abstract: Embryonic stem cells (ESCs) are thought to maintain pluripotency through global hyper-transcription, linked to an "open" chromatin structure. To investigate this idea, we analyzed higher-order chromatin fibers from mouse ESCs, their differentiated progenitors, and terminally differentiated mouse NIH3T3 fibroblasts. Bulk chromatin composition, including protein:DNA ratio and nucleosome repeat length, varied little between the cell types; however, surprisingly, biophysical analyses, such as fluorescence recovery after photobleaching of linker histones, hydrodynamic sedimentation, and nuclease sensitivity, also showed no significant differences in the conformation of purified higher-order chromatin fibers. To better evaluate the structure of higher-order chromatin fibers observed in cells, we developed a novel technique called SPOCC (sedimentation properties of cross-linked chromatin). This approach revealed that ESCs and differentiated cells share similar bulk higher-order chromatin fiber structures, while ESCs have a slightly more disrupted structure than NIH3T3cell chromatin. These results indicate that ESC transcriptional activity and plasticity are not driven by a fundamentally "open" higher-order chromatin conformation.

supplemented_raw_records.title: Diet-attributable colorectal cancer in Asia: Regional heterogeneity in burden and dietary intake
supplemented_raw_records.abstract: Colorectal cancer incidence is rising rapidly in Asia, with dietary factors being major modifiable risk factors. We assessed disability-adjusted life years (DALYs), mortality, age-standardized DALY rate (ASDR), age-standardized mortality rate (ASMR), estimated annual percentage change, and population-attributable fraction using Global Burden of Disease 2023 data. Spatial alignment between 2018 Global Dietary Database intake and 2018 attributable ASDR was examined using Spearman correlation and bivariate maps. High-income Asia Pacific recorded the highest diet-attributable ASDR and ASMR in 2023, while South Asia recorded the lowest. Among Asian subregions, High-income Asia Pacific recorded the highest ASDRs attributable to diets low in whole grains, high in red meat, and high in processed meat. Within each subregion, diets low in whole grains or milk generally ranked first. Whole grains, milk, calcium, and fiber showed clearer spatial alignment. Given the heterogeneity of diet-attributable burden in Asia, region-specific dietary prevention strategies should be prioritized.

supplemented_raw_records.title: Plastic shifts in web architecture alter signal physics and influence collective behavior and ecological prevalence
supplemented_raw_records.abstract: Many animals build external sensory structures, yet how these extended phenotypes shape information transmission, behavior and population outcomes remains poorly understood. We investigated a social spider whose web architecture shifts from multiplanar 3D webs on vegetation to planar 2D webs on anthropogenic substrates. Field vibration measurements revealed signal trade-offs: 2D webs transmit fast-but-noisy signals that trigger rapid collective recruitment, whereas 3D webs transmit slower, clearer signals enabling precise hunting by fewer individuals. Despite capturing similar total prey and suffering higher mortality while attacking dangerous prey (17% of natural diet), 2D colonies produced more clutches, grew larger, and were more prevalent in fence-modified habitats. Playback experiments confirmed that fast signals causally amplify collective recruitment, while mechanistic models showed that differences in web topology reproduce qualitative signal regimes across web types. Therefore, simple topological shifts in extended phenotypes reshape microscale signal properties, biasing collective responses that scale to fitness and ecological outcomes.

supplemented_raw_records.title: European robin cryptochrome 4a does not bind 8-HDF or MTHF as second antenna chromophores
supplemented_raw_records.abstract: Cryptochromes and photolyases are blue-light-sensitive flavoproteins that generally bind flavin adenine dinucleotide (FAD) and have distinct functions. Cryptochrome 4a (CRY4a) expressed in the double-cone photoreceptors of migratory songbirds such as the European robin ( Erithacus rubecula ) is the hypothesized primary sensor for avian magnetoreception. In addition to FAD, many photolyases and some cryptochromes bind antenna chromophores such as 8-hydroxy-5-deazaflavin (8-HDF) or 5,10-methenyltetrahydrofolate (MTHF). Here, we investigated whether  Erithacus rubecula  cryptochrome 4a ( Er CRY4a) also binds 8-HDF and/or MTHF. 8-HDF binding was tested by co-expressing  Er CRY4a with 8-HDF synthase. 8-HDF bound the positive control  Xenopus laevis  6-4 photolyase ( Xl 6-4PL), but not  Er CRY4a. For MTHF, the positive control  Escherichia coli  DNA photolyase ( Ec DPL) was purified with both MTHF and FAD, whereas  Er CRY4a showed only FAD binding. Isothermal titration calorimetry also confirmed that MTHF does not bind  Er CRY4a. Furthermore, computational analysis revealed no binding-site similarity between  Er CRY4a and MTHF/8-HDF-binding proteins, indicating a non-conserved pocket.

supplemented_raw_records.title: PADI2 facilitates progression and cisplatin resistance of epithelial ovarian cancer via m6A methylation
supplemented_raw_records.abstract: Chemotherapy resistance is a challenge in the management of epithelial ovarian cancer (EOC). The regulation of N6-methyladenosine (m6A) RNA modification has emerged as a potential strategy to overcome this resistance. Peptidyl Arginine Deiminase 2 ( PADI2 ) was found to be upregulated and highly methylated in EOC samples, correlating with a poor prognosis. Downregulation of  PADI2  inhibited colony formation, cell proliferation, and cisplatin (cDDP) resistance in EOC cells.  METTL3  was identified as the m6A writer of  PADI2  mRNA, while  YTHDF2  recognized and bound the m6A-methylated  PADI2  mRNA, enhancing its translation. This activation of the JAK2/STAT3 pathway facilitated cDDP resistance in EOC cells both  in vitro  and  in vivo . Knockdown of  METTL3  or  YTHDF2  decreased  PADI2  mRNA expression and suppressed tumor growth and cDDP resistance. In conclusion, a mechanism was identified whereby m6A-modified  PADI2  induces cDDP resistance and EOC progression, providing a potential target for the development of therapeutic strategies for EOC treatment.

supplemented_raw_records.title: Hydrogen adsorption and dissociation on late transition metal doped C24/C2N heterostructure
supplemented_raw_records.abstract: Hydrogen dissociation is essential for many hydrogen-related applications and requires efficient catalysts based on earth-abundant elements. Through density functional theory (DFT) calculations, the effect of the late first-row transition metals on H 2  activation and dissociation was investigated on single-atom catalysts supported on a C 24 /C 2 N heterostructure. Metal-support interactions, H 2  adsorption, dissociation pathways, activation barriers, and electronic structures were systematically evaluated. The metal-support interaction was found to be the strongest for Fe@C 24 /C 2 N (-5.09 eV), and the dissociation barrier for H 2  was the lowest for Ni@C 24 /C 2 N (0.23 eV). The molecular-level understanding of bonding and charge transfer during H 2  activation was gained using non-covalent interactions (NCI), quantum theory of atoms in molecules (QTAIM), natural bond orbital (NBO), and electron-density-difference analyses. The molecular dynamics simulations further supported the structural stability of the selected systems under the simulated conditions. These results elucidate the relationship between the type of transition metal, the nature of the interaction with the support, and the activation of H 2 , and offer guidance for the development of catalysts for hydrogen-related applications.

supplemented_raw_records.title: HDAC2 modulation of KCC2 in the anterior cingulate cortex impairs synaptic plasticity in chronic neuropathic pain with cognitive impairment
supplemented_raw_records.abstract: This study explores the role of histone deacetylase 2 (HDAC2) in the anterior cingulate cortex (ACC) in chronic pain-related cognitive impairment following chronic constriction injury (CCI). Behavioral tests, molecular analyses, and neuronal morphology assessments revealed that HDAC2 expression was markedly increased in the ACC of CCI mice, accompanied by reduced dendritic spine density and cognitive deficits. Pharmacological inhibition or small interfering RNA (siRNA)-mediated knockdown of HDAC2 alleviated pain hypersensitivity and improved cognition, whereas adeno-associated virus (AAV)-mediated HDAC2 overexpression induced similar pathological features in naive mice. Moreover, HDAC2 upregulation suppressed potassium-chloride cotransporter 2 (KCC2) expression, suggesting that HDAC2 modulates synaptic plasticity through epigenetic repression of KCC2. Restoration of KCC2 expression or inhibition of HDAC2 rescued dendritic abnormalities and behavioral impairments. Restoration of KCC2 activity via the specific agonist CLP257 rescued dendritic spine abnormalities, normalized ACC neuronal hyperexcitability, and alleviated both pain and cognitive impairment in CCI mice. These findings indicate that HDAC2 contributes to neuropathic pain-related cognitive dysfunction by epigenetically suppressing KCC2, which in turn impairs synaptic plasticity and disrupts neuronal excitability in the ACC.

supplemented_raw_records.title: Characterization of lysine methylation during neuronal differentiation of LUHMES cells
supplemented_raw_records.abstract: Over one-third of human lysine methyltransferases (KMTs) and lysine demethylases (KDMs) are linked to neurodevelopmental disorders (NDDs). Changes in histone lysine methylation during neuronal differentiation have been reported. It is now recognized that KMTs and KDMs also target non-histone proteins, yet characterization of non-histone lysine methylation during neuronal differentiation remains limited. Here, we address this gap using quantitative mass spectrometry-based proteomics to quantify changes in non-histone lysine methylation across three stages of the Lund human mesencephalic (LUHMES) neuronal differentiation model. We identify 70 lysine methylation events with significant differences in abundance across differentiation. Our analysis reveals lysine methylation on many non-histone proteins involved in neuronal differentiation, including signaling molecules, cytoskeletal proteins, RNA splicing factors, and transcription factors. This work broadens the understanding of non-histone lysine methylation in a neuronal differentiation model and provides a resource of lysine methylation sites on proteins of biological and clinical significance for future research.

supplemented_raw_records.title: Retinal Müller glial nestin reduction parallels behavioral impairment after blue light exposure in rats
supplemented_raw_records.abstract: Blue light from light-emitting diode (LED) displays is widely encountered; however, its effects beyond the retina are poorly understood. We investigated whether short-term blue light exposure alters retinal Müller glial nestin immunoreactivity and whether these changes accompany behavioral changes. Male Wistar rats were exposed to blue light (450 nm, 4 h daily) for 7 (D-7) or 14 days and compared with controls. Passive avoidance and elevated plus maze tests showed impaired memory retention and increased anxiety-like behavior, whereas rotarod performance was reduced at 7-D but not at 14-D. Immunofluorescence showed a progressive decline in nestin signal in the inner nuclear layer, which correlated with a composite behavioral deficit score across animals. These data reveal a temporal association between changes in Müller glial markers and behavioral outcomes, identifying the glial marker nestin as a candidate indicator of light-induced stress and motivating mechanistic studies.

supplemented_raw_records.title: SARS-CoV-2 infection and genomic diversity in Quilombola communities during Brazil’s gamma VOC wave
supplemented_raw_records.abstract: COVID-19 has disproportionately affected vulnerable populations worldwide; yet, data on SARS-CoV-2 transmission and variant diversity in Brazil's descendants of enslaved individuals, known as Quilombola, remain scarce. We conducted a cross-sectional study in Cachoeira, Bahia, in people seeking care, between February and March 2021, testing 700 oropharyngeal swabs by RT-qPCR and 591 plasma samples for IgM/IgG antibodies. Positive samples with Cq < 25 underwent genomic sequencing and phylogenetic analysis. SARS-CoV-2 infection burden was comparable between urban (31.4%) and rural (32.0%) zones in Quilombola communities. Genomic analysis of 39 sequences identified multiple lineages, predominantly the Gamma variant (P.1), with phylogenetic evidence of numerous introductions and both local and external transmission. These results reveal complex transmission dynamics and variant diversity within marginalized Quilombola populations, underscoring the need for targeted public health interventions, expanded diagnostic coverage, and prioritization of these communities in vaccination campaigns to address health inequities.

supplemented_raw_records.title: Targeted degradation of a constitutively active GPCR oncoprotein
supplemented_raw_records.abstract: To assess the feasibility of using proteolysis-targeting chimeras (PROTACs) to target G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs), we constructed a degron-tagged GPCR library in which a HaloTag7 protein fusion tag was engineered into the cytoplasmic carboxyl terminal tail. We used luciferase complementation and immunoblot assays to quantify cellular receptor protein levels after treatment with a von Hippel-Lindau (VHL) E3 ligase-recruiting bifunctional molecule, HaloPROTAC3. HaloPROTAC3 treatment resulted in recruitment of the VHL E3 ligase, yielding a time- and dose-dependent decrease in receptor expression and decreased agonist-dependent receptor signaling. We then focused on human cysteinyl leukotriene receptor 2 (CysLTR2). The CysLTR2 mutant L129Q constitutively signals through heterotrimeric G proteins and drives tumorigenesis in uveal melanoma (UM). We observed a HaloPROTAC3 dose-dependent decrease in receptor levels in primary human melanocytes expressing the engineered CysLTR2-L129Q mutant. Our results support the potential utility of using PROTACs as GPCR degraders.

supplemented_raw_records.title: Exercise imprints a persistent tumor intrinsic suppressive state in colorectal cancer
supplemented_raw_records.abstract: Exercise reduces colorectal cancer (CRC) progression, yet whether it acts directly and durably on tumor cells has been difficult to establish. Using syngeneic murine models, we show that aerobic exercise training suppresses primary tumor growth, pulmonary metastasis, and cachexia, and imprints a tumor-intrinsic suppressive state that persists  ex vivo . Tumor cells from exercised mice retain reduced growth after serial transplantation into untrained hosts, and tumors of exercised mice show reduced expression of a subset of microRNAs and of their biogenesis machinery, including  Dicer . This state is accompanied by intracellular serine depletion and a steady-state metabolite signature consistent with reduced glycolytic biosynthesis and increased mitochondrial substrate use. Across human CRC cohorts, lower  DICER1  expression is associated with better clinical outcome, paralleling the exercise-conditioned state. These findings indicate that exercise can impose a persistent, tumor-intrinsic regulatory and metabolic constraint, broadening the conceptual basis for physical activity in cancer biology.

supplemented_raw_records.title: Hierarchical multivariate analysis identifies dominant and secondary patterns in oral bacteria-host autophagy networks in oral squamous cell carcinoma
supplemented_raw_records.abstract: Oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) progression has been increasingly linked to dysbiosis of the oral microbiome. We hypothesized that pathogenic versus commensal bacteria are associated with distinct host autophagy-network architectures that may favor inflammatory/invasive or homeostatic/proteostatic signaling in OSCC. To test this, we constructed literature-derived host-bacterium autophagy interactomes from KEGG, STRING, and curated databases, identifying key network hubs (e.g., MAPK1 and STAT3) via graph-theoretic metrics. We then applied principal component analysis, permutation testing, and linear discriminant analysis (LDA) to interrogate network topology. This framework revealed an outlier-dominated rather than binary PCA structure: Fusobacterium nucleatum and Streptococcus mitis were the most separated taxa, while the remaining bacteria formed a compact central cluster. Pathobiont-associated networks emphasized inflammatory-metabolic autophagy signatures, whereas commensal-associated networks emphasized kinase-homeostasis signaling. Permutation testing and degree-preserving randomization confirmed that the explained-variance structure was non-random ( p < 0.001; Z = 19.13). Leave-one-out and bootstrap analyses supported variance robustness and recurrent gene contributions without establishing a stable signature. The Dysbiosis Index distinguished the bacterial cohorts but requires independent validation. Clinical datasets provided supportive but indirect relevance and showed concurrent activation of pathogenic and homeostatic programs. Collectively, these findings provide a hypothesis-generating framework requiring mechanistic and clinical validation.

supplemented_raw_records.title: Chemogenetic hyperpolarization in the entorhinal cortex during sleep facilitates delta oscillations and memory consolidation
supplemented_raw_records.abstract: Memory consolidation is a crucial step in long-term memory formation, during which stable memory representations are formed using recently encoded labile memories. The entorhinal cortex (EC) mediates such brain-wide memory reorganization by exhibiting delta oscillations during sleep, through hyperpolarization-activated cyclic nucleotide-gated (HCN) channels. We tested the feasibility of chemogenetically manipulating EC delta oscillations and examined whether such manipulations affect memory consolidation. We demonstrate that membrane hyperpolarization via the activation of the inhibitory chemogenetic receptor hM4Di paradoxically facilitates delta oscillations in the EC by activating HCN channels, whereas membrane depolarization via the activation of the excitatory chemogenetic receptor hM3Dq induces the opposite effect. Furthermore, we show that chemogenetic depolarization during sleep following learning impairs memory consolidation, whereas chemogenetic hyperpolarization enhances it. Our study provides insights into the effects of chemogenetic manipulation on neural oscillations and identifies EC delta as a key regulator of memory consolidation efficiency.

supplemented_raw_records.title: Cell-type specific modulation of dorsal raphe serotonergic neurons by ketamine
supplemented_raw_records.abstract: Ketamine (KET) produces rapid and long-lasting antidepressant effects at subanesthetic doses. However, the underlying mechanisms by which KET regulates the function of dorsal raphe nucleus (DRN) serotonergic neurons, a key brain area involved in the regulation of emotional behaviors, including depression, remain largely unknown. Here, we show that KET increases the firing activity of DRN serotonergic neurons while bidirectionally modulating their excitatory inputs in a cell-type-specific manner. Retrograde circuit mapping reveals that KET preferentially potentiates glutamatergic synapses of DRN 5-HT neurons projecting to the medial prefrontal cortex while depressing glutamate synapses of those projecting to the central amygdala (CeA). Notably, KET-induced synaptic potentiation in the DRN-but not the increase in serotonergic neuronal firing-was abolished by blockade of the brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF) receptor tyrosine kinase B (TrkB). These findings indicate the presence of parallel TrkB-dependent and TrkB-independent signaling pathways that regulate DRN serotonergic neuron function.

supplemented_raw_records.title: Identification and validation of serum EPHB2 as a candidate biomarker for colorectal cancer and precancerous lesions
supplemented_raw_records.abstract: This study identifies and validates serum EPHB2 as a non-invasive candidate biomarker for early detection of colorectal cancer (CRC) and precancerous adenomas. Through integrative analysis of multi-cohort transcriptomics, pan-cancer databases, and single-cell RNA sequencing, EPHB2 was identified as a CRC-specific marker predominantly localized to malignant epithelial cells, with expression progressively elevated from precancerous lesions through advanced carcinoma. Clinical ELISA validation in prospective local and independent external cohorts, supported by tissue immunohistochemistry, demonstrated robust diagnostic performance across both cohorts: serum EPHB2 achieved AUCs of 0.794-0.839 for adenoma detection and 0.816-0.897 for distinguishing CRC from healthy controls, and effectively discriminated neoplastic from benign inflammatory lesions (AUCs of 0.817-0.874). Mechanistic analyses further revealed that EPHB2 expression is associated with Wnt/β-catenin signaling activation in colorectal tumorigenesis. Collectively, these findings establish serum EPHB2 as a promising candidate biomarker that warrants further prospective evaluation for early detection of colorectal neoplasia.

supplemented_raw_records.title: Agentic finance and sustainability: governing autonomous capital allocation for societal benefit
Nested paradoxes around how biodiversity constrains business: Why biodiversity conservation requires paradox thinking
supplemented_raw_records.abstract: Mounting evidence of nature degradation has led governmental and non-governmental actors to put pressure on companies to address their impact on biodiversity, as their economic value creation contributes directly or indirectly to biodiversity loss. However, designing effective mitigation measures requires acknowledging the complex interplay of political, social, and economic constraints that shape corporate decision-making. We elucidate how a paradox perspective provides a productive way of understanding corporate biodiversity engagement, or the absence thereof. Specifically, we illuminate how corporate biodiversity engagement is shaped by nested paradoxes operating at all levels of the economic system, wherein responses to higher-level paradoxes structurally constrain possible responses to lower-level paradoxes. We argue that meaningful corporate biodiversity engagement necessitates concerted actions across all levels, thereby empowering companies to engage with biodiversity in a proactive and consequential manner.

supplemented_raw_records.title: PyFCG: A Python toolkit for constructionist language processing and learning
supplemented_raw_records.abstract: This article introduces PyFCG, an open-source scientific software toolkit that enables its users to efficiently integrate state-of-the-art constructionist language processing and learning into larger Python projects. The toolkit provides a fully Pythonic interface to the leading computational construction grammar framework, Fluid Construction Grammar (FCG), facilitating its swift integration with Python's rich ecosystem of libraries, in particular those implementing today's most popular machine learning techniques. Apart from a general description of the toolkit, this article provides three illustrative case studies that demonstrate how PyFCG facilitates (i) the formalization and computational operationalization of construction grammar analyses, (ii) the learning of usage-based construction grammars from corpora of language use, and (iii) the implementation of multi-agent emergent communication experiments that combine symbolic and neural computation.

supplemented_raw_records.title: Distinct cellular mechanisms underlie ON orientation selectivity in the mouse retina
supplemented_raw_records.abstract: Orientation selectivity (OS) is a fundamental visual computation. We characterized three morphophysiologically distinct ON orientation-selective ganglion cell (OSGC) populations in the mouse retina: S345 OSGCs and two less frequently recorded groups, putative S13 and S15 OSGCs. Mechanistic analyses focused on S345 OSGCs, which exhibited robust orientation tuning and continuous dendritic stratification across inner plexiform layer strata S3-S5. Their OS depended on a tetrodotoxin (TTX)-sensitive GABAergic inhibitory surround. TTX abolished orientation tuning, whereas 2,3-dihydroxy-6-nitro-7-sulfamoylbenzo[f]quinoxaline (NBQX) reduced orientation-dependent inhibition and eliminated OS, implicating AMPA/kainate receptor-dependent recruitment of spiking inhibitory circuits. Physiologically identified spiking orientation-selective amacrine cells exhibited asymmetric inward-current responses, with orientation bias persisting in TTX. These findings expand the known diversity of ON orientation-selective retinal neurons, suggest distinct patterns of excitation and inhibition underlying their orientation signals, and identify a spiking GABAergic inhibitory mechanism shaping OS in S345 OSGCs.

supplemented_raw_records.title: Hippocampal tangential insertions of high-density silicon probes in head- fixed mice enhance spatial sampling
supplemented_raw_records.abstract: The hippocampus is a key structure within the medial temporal lobe, which plays a central role in the formation and consolidation of declarative memories. Due to its complex croissant-like morphology, it has been difficult to use linear high-density probes to perform extracellular recordings from large continuous segments of the hippocampus. We here describe how to apply a tangential insertion approach to enable continuous recordings of the hippocampus. We propose two different insertions aligned to either the dorsal or ventral sections of the hippocampus. Both insertions are performed in head-fixed conditions, which can be easily combined with detailed monitoring of the animals' behavioral states. We show that when placed across the pyramidal layer, they can harness ripple oscillations at an unprecedented spatial resolution, which also enabled us to record up to 400 hippocampal neurons simultaneously from a single probe, endowing us with the capability to capture putative functionally connected neuronal pairs.

supplemented_raw_records.title: Consequences of climate-driven relocation in the Prehispanic US Southwest
supplemented_raw_records.abstract: As humanity copes with a warming planet, there is a growing recognition that in some situations entire communities may be forced to relocate. This perspective paper summarizes an especially well-understood episode of climate-driven relocation that took place in the Four Corners region of the US Southwest in the 13 th  century CE. This episode is well understood due to an exceptional archaeological record with high temporal resolution, oral traditions that have been maintained in descendant communities, a long history of research, and significant investment in synthesis of both archaeological and paleoclimatic records. The account is also well established in that it is based on a robust quantity and quality of evidence and high agreement among experts. The account is organized around questions that are often raised regarding community relocation in the present, thus providing an example of how archaeological research can contribute to the knowledge base for successful climate change adaptation responses today.

supplemented_raw_records.title: LKMHCpan: Transformer-optimized HLA-I pseudo-sequences enhance neoantigen prediction for immunotherapy
supplemented_raw_records.abstract: Accurate peptide-HLA class I binding prediction is fundamental for identifying tumor neoantigens and advancing personalized immunotherapy. We present LKMHCpan, a pan-specific predictor that leverages transformer networks to optimize HLA-I pseudo-sequences representation through attention-guided integration of 88 key residues primarily within the α1, α2, and α3 domains. LKMHCpan achieves a mean precision-recall area under the curve (PR-AUC) of 0.93, generalizes robustly to untrained HLA-I alleles, and supports peptides longer than 11 amino acids. In Tumor Neoantigen Selection Alliance (TESLA) data, LKMHCpan identified 94% of immunogenic neoantigens with strong score-immunogenicity correlation. Neoantigen burden from LKMHCpan significantly stratified clinical outcomes in two immunotherapy-treated cohorts: metastatic melanoma ( n  = 73) and lung cancer ( n  = 309), with high-burden patients exhibiting clinical benefit. Its ability to resolve binding motifs for untrained alleles and single-amino-acid HLA-I mutants highlights its potential for elucidating complex peptide-major histocompatibility complex (MHC) interactions. LKMHCpan provides a scalable framework for neoantigen discovery and prognostic assessment in precision immunotherapy.

supplemented_raw_records.title: Notch-mediated thyroid hormone regulation of skin development in the zebrafish caudal fin
supplemented_raw_records.abstract: Thyroid hormone (TH) is a systemic regulator of vertebrate development. Although TH is known to be involved in the maturation of stratified skin, this role has remained incompletely understood. Using the skin at the peripheral-most edge of the zebrafish caudal fin, we characterized the trajectory of epidermal maturation during the transition from juvenile to adult. We found that TH regulates the allometric expansion of the peripheral edge (PE) by stimulating both cell proliferation and hypertrophy of the epidermis. We further demonstrated that TH acts upstream of the Notch pathway to mediate this expansion. While TH signaling machinery was broadly expressed throughout the fin, effectors of the Notch pathway were specifically enriched in the PE. Inhibiting Notch activity prevented PE expansion, while upregulating Notch partially rescued the effects of TH deficiency. Identifying Notch as a highly region-specific effector of TH-driven growth, our findings reveal a mechanism by which systemic endocrine signals may be translated into local tissue-level skin morphogenesis.

supplemented_raw_records.title: White-tailed deer milk promotes rapid SARS-CoV-2 RNA degradation through synergistic ionic and enzymatic mechanisms
supplemented_raw_records.abstract: White-tailed deer ( Odocoileus virginianus , WTD), the most extensively documented SARS-CoV-2 wildlife host in North America, undergo seasonal lactation that constitutes a direct yet uninvestigated pathway for viral exposure at the maternal-offspring interface. Here, we report the first detection of SARS-CoV-2-specific neutralizing antibodies in wildlife milk and demonstrate that WTD milk rapidly degrades viral RNA from three SARS-CoV-2 variants (lineages A, B.1.1.7, and BA.1.1.529) within 10 min at physiological temperatures, while human milk permits viral RNA persistence. Mechanistic interrogation revealed 5- to 20-fold elevated mineral concentrations, 3- to 5-fold enhanced protease activity, and substantially higher lactoperoxidase levels in WTD milk. Synergistic interactions among these ionic, proteolytic, and enzymatic factors drive variant-specific RNA degradation. Functional reconstitution of human milk with lactoperoxidase and a WTD-matched ionic formulation recapitulated the antiviral phenotype, establishing the mechanistic sufficiency of this biochemical axis. These findings identify species-specific milk biochemistry as a previously unrecognized determinant of viral fate during lactation.

supplemented_raw_records.title: Adaptive gating-based fusion of sequential and local features for predicting drug-drug interactions
supplemented_raw_records.abstract: Accurate prediction of drug-drug interactions (DDIs) is important for reducing risks associated with polypharmacy and adverse drug reactions. To overcome the limitations of experimental methods, we present AGSL-DDI, an end-to-end framework that learns interaction representations directly from SMILES sequences. Character-level embeddings are processed in parallel by a bidirectional long short-term memory network and a one-dimensional convolutional neural network to capture complementary global sequential dependencies and local chemical patterns. An adaptive gating mechanism dynamically integrates these features, while bidirectional multi-head cross-attention models fine-grained interactions between paired drugs. On the BioSNAP and DrugBank datasets, AGSL-DDI achieved AUROC values of 0.9852 and 0.9816 and AUPR values of 0.9837 and 0.9818, respectively. These results show that coordinated global-local representation learning and cross-drug interaction modeling can effectively characterize DDI patterns, providing a practical computational approach for medication risk screening and drug development.

supplemented_raw_records.title: Astrocytic mitochondria restore neuronal bioenergetics and function in Parkinson disease models
supplemented_raw_records.abstract: Mitochondrial dysfunction contributes to neuronal injury in Parkinson's disease, and astrocyte-derived mitochondria may offer neuroprotection by restoring neuronal bioenergetics. Here, we investigated the therapeutic potential of astrocyte-derived mitochondria in 6-OHDA models of Parkinson's disease. Using mitochondrial labeling and co-culture assays, we obtained evidence consistent with the release of astrocytic mitochondria, their uptake by injured neurons, and their association with the neuronal mitochondrial network. Building on this observation, we investigated whether direct delivery of functional astrocytic mitochondria could augment endogenous support during neuronal injury. Infused astrocytic mitochondria reduced oxidative stress, restored mitochondrial membrane potential, improved mitochondrial respiration, normalized calcium homeostasis, reduced early neuronal apoptosis, and restored mitochondrial mass. Astrocytic mitochondrial delivery enhanced dendritic arborization in primary neurons.  In vivo , stereotactic infusion restored TH immunoreactivity in the SNpc and improved motor and non-motor behavioral deficits. These findings support the potential of astrocyte-derived mitochondria as a promising cell-free therapeutic approach for Parkinson's disease.

supplemented_raw_records.title: Environmental phthalate and chronic kidney disease: Epidemiology, mechanistic pathways, and clinical implications
supplemented_raw_records.abstract: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) remains a major global health problem, and early detection and risk control are still limited. Phthalates-widely used plasticizers with endocrine-disrupting effects-have been increasingly implicated in CKD-related outcomes. Human studies have reported associations between urinary phthalate metabolites and kidney-related markers, commonly reflected by the albumin-to-creatinine ratio (ACR) and estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR), although the direction and magnitude of these associations vary by metabolite, population, study design, and outcome definition. Mechanistic evidence is currently dominated by studies of di-(2-ethylhexyl) phthalate (DEHP) and its metabolite mono-(2-ethylhexyl) phthalate (MEHP), suggesting potential involvement of oxidative stress, inflammation, regulated cell death, epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT), and extracellular-matrix (ECM) remodeling in experimental models. However, the extent to which these mechanisms apply to other phthalates or alternative plasticizers remains uncertain. The evidence remains heterogeneous across populations and exposure contexts, and key limitations include its observational nature, exposure-measurement bias, reverse causality, and uncertainty regarding temporality and mixture effects. Future longitudinal, pharmacokinetic, and intervention studies are needed to determine whether phthalate biomarkers have clinically meaningful prognostic or predictive utility.

supplemented_raw_records.title: NADPH phosphatase activity of Mesh1 contributes to sleep regulation in Drosophila
supplemented_raw_records.abstract: Metazoans possess Mesh1, an enzyme with both ppGpp hydrolase and NADPH phosphatase activities, raising questions about their respective physiological roles. To distinguish these functions, we combined biochemical characterization, structure-guided mutagenesis, genome editing, and behavioral analysis in Drosophila . We found that Drosophila Mesh1 dephosphorylates NADPH but not NADP + in vitro . Substitution of tryptophan 138 with phenylalanine (W138F) abolished detectable NADPH phosphatase activity while retaining detectable but severely reduced ppGpp hydrolase activity. Flies carrying the W138F mutation exhibited reduced total sleep duration and increased sleep fragmentation. These findings implicate the NADPH phosphatase activity of Mesh1 in sleep regulation and identify W138 as a critical residue for this function. Our results highlight a physiological role for Mesh1 beyond ppGpp metabolism and suggest a connection between NADPH metabolism and the regulation of sleep in metazoans.

supplemented_raw_records.title: Multiomic crosstalk between plasma metabolites and inflammation in IBD via MR and mouse validation
supplemented_raw_records.abstract: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is a chronic relapsing inflammatory disorder characterized by gut dysbiosis and recurrent intestinal inflammation. Integrating bibliometric analysis, two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR), cross-platform protein pQTL MR, colocalization, and druggability assessment, we dissected gut microbiota-driven plasma metabolite-inflammation homeostasis axes in IBD. MR and mediation analyses identified multi-omics biomarkers and 24 candidate therapeutic metabolites organized into three regulatory axes: Klebsiella-glycine-β-muricholic acid (Gly-β-MCA)-CCL20/IL-10RA, Clostridium sp CAG-632-lauroyl-L-carnitine chloride-IL-10/IL-8, and Treponema-4-vinylphenol-IL-10RA. In RAW 264.7 macrophages and dextran sulfate sodium (DSS)- and 2,4,6-trinitrobenzene sulfonic acid (TNBS)-induced colitis models in mice, the three metabolites suppressed pro-inflammatory cytokine expression, with Gly-β-MCA showing the strongest effect and lauroyl-L-carnitine chloride upregulating IL-10 to alleviate Crohn's-like colitis. These findings help clarify multi-omics causal relationships in IBD and support precision anti-inflammatory therapy via metabolite-inflammation axes.

supplemented_raw_records.title: Intra-DNA k-mer conservation patterns encode evolutionary selection of variants
supplemented_raw_records.abstract: Current approaches to variant effect prediction center on protein function and interspecies conservation, largely ignoring cues embedded in local nucleotide composition. We developed kGain, a metric that quantifies how a point mutation reshapes oligonucleotide frequency relative to the host genome. In  Escherichia coli  and  Saccharomyces cerevisiae  long-term evolution data, fixed, essential-gene, and recurrent mutations carry elevated kGain values that grow more pronounced over successive generations. Parallel trends appear in SARS-CoV-2 variants of concern and in a bottleneck resistance experiment, where a high-kGain  fusA  Y515N change conferred antibiotic resistance at no detectable fitness cost. A transformer regressor trained on one strain transfers accurately to others, indicating that the compositional rules kGain captures are broadly conserved and offering a new sequence-intrinsic dimension for understanding adaptive selection.

supplemented_raw_records.title: RNA-binding proteome dynamics following ischemia-reperfusion injury in the kidney
supplemented_raw_records.abstract: Acute kidney injury (AKI) is a frequent complication in hospitalized patients and is associated with increased mortality. Despite its relevance, no targeted therapies are available. RNA-binding proteins (RBPs) are essential regulators of cellular function and have been implicated in AKI, but a comprehensive analysis of their role is lacking. We investigated RBP regulation in porcine kidneys subjected to ischemia-reperfusion injury following cardiopulmonary resuscitation. To assess evolutionary conservation, RBP profiles were also obtained from human kidney tissue. After ischemia-reperfusion injury, we found RBPs exhibiting altered RNA-binding capacity, including metabolic enzymes previously implicated in ischemic stress. These findings suggest that energy metabolism is linked to RNA regulation during kidney injury. Renal ischemia-reperfusion injury alters the RNA-binding landscape, affecting both regulatory and metabolic RBPs. The conservation of these proteins in human kidneys highlights their translational relevance and identifies RNA-protein interactions as potential therapeutic targets in AKI.

supplemented_raw_records.title: The RNA and protein landscapes of mouse brain organoids
supplemented_raw_records.abstract: Organoids are powerful models of brain development and function. Mouse brain organoids reproduce the main steps of neurodevelopment  in vivo  and differentiate more rapidly than human organoids, making them scalable for screening applications. However, mouse brain organoids remain poorly defined. Here, we showed that the transcriptome and proteome of mouse brain organoids developed for three weeks are close to those of a neonatal mouse brain. Strikingly, organoids recapitulated the majority of alternative splicing and polyadenylation-site events that define neural identity  in vivo . Proteomics revealed that most changes in mRNA expression were translated into proteins. Mouse brain organoids differentiated for only three weeks already harbored a complex network of synaptic proteins, including the ionotropic and metabotropic receptors for the neurotransmitters glutamate and GABA. To conclude, our study provides evidence that mouse brain organoids are a rapidly maturing and relevant model of mammalian brain development and function in a neonatal-like environment.

supplemented_raw_records.title: Solution-processed Ti3C2Tx MXene coatings for three-dimensional microelectrodes in label-free single-cell impedance spectroscopy
supplemented_raw_records.abstract: Three-dimensional (3D) microelectrodes may improve electric-field coupling to confined cells, but their fabrication often requires complex metallization or specialized equipment. Here, we decouple topography formation from conductive functionalization by combining solvent-induced swelling of cyclic olefin copolymer (COC) with solution-processed Ti 3 C 2 T x  MXene (TMX) coating. Swelling generated COC features approximately 10 μm high, while spin-coated TMX formed an approximately 80 nm conformal conductive layer. The electrodes were integrated into a constriction-based microfluidic device and compared with 3D Au electrodes fabricated on the same swollen COC architecture. Simulations showed field localization across the constriction for both materials. Replicated differential impedance measurements of more than 20 individually trapped MDA-MB-231 cells per material, using three independently fabricated devices per material, showed increased low-frequency impedance relative to cell-free medium. Although Au produced smoother spectra and stronger absolute separation, TMX generated measurable cell-associated responses, demonstrating a solution-processable route to 3D microfluidic bioelectrodes for label-free single-cell sensing.

supplemented_raw_records.title: A proteomic map of B cell activation and its shaping by mTORC1, MYC and iron
supplemented_raw_records.abstract: Using high-resolution quantitative mass spectrometry, we explored how immune activation and the metabolic regulator mTORC1 shape the B cell proteome. Activation through the B cell receptor, CD40, and the IL-4 receptor caused extensive remodeling of the protein landscape, including increased expression of metabolic machinery and nutrient transporters needed to support growth and biosynthesis. Comparing T cell-dependent and T cell-independent stimulation identified both shared and distinct pathways driving these changes. Inhibition of mTORC1 revealed an essential role in activation-induced B cell growth, amino acid transporter expression, and protein production. mTORC1 also regulated expression of the transcription factor MYC and the transferrin receptor CD71. Inhibiting MYC largely mirrored the effects of mTORC1 inhibition, while reduced iron availability impaired B cell growth and protein synthesis. These findings provide a comprehensive map of B cell proteome remodeling and reveal key roles for mTORC1, MYC and iron in supporting activation-induced growth and protein production.

supplemented_raw_records.title: Clinical, molecular, and immune correlates of TmS in patients with platinum-pretreated advanced bladder carcinoma receiving atezolizumab
Modeling congenital cytomegalovirus infection in human inner ear organoids
supplemented_raw_records.abstract: Congenital infection with human cytomegalovirus is a leading cause of congenital hearing loss. Investigating its effects is challenging due to the virus's strict species specificity, limiting the relevance of animal models. This study aimed to establish a human-specific model of cytomegalovirus infection in the developing inner ear using inner ear organoids derived from pluripotent stem cells. Organoids were cultured for 75 days, vibratome sectioned into 300-μm slices, and exposed to laboratory or clinical strains of human cytomegalovirus for 7 or 21 days. Viral replication was confirmed, with successful infection by clinical strains requiring a minimum viral titer. Immunofluorescence revealed targeted infection of nonsensory epithelial cells and mesenchymal cells, with occasional infection of hair cells and neurons. This model replicates the key aspects of congenital cytomegalovirus infection, providing a scalable human platform to study viral pathogenesis, identify susceptible cell types, and explore targeted therapies.

supplemented_raw_records.title: YAP dosage controls anteroposterior axis elongation in human 3D gastruloids
supplemented_raw_records.abstract: Human embryonic stem cell (hESC)-derived three-dimensional gastruloids (h3D-gastruloids) recapitulate key features of early human embryogenesis, including germ layer formation, symmetry breaking, and establishment of the body plan. Here, we investigate the role of the Hippo pathway effector YAP in human gastruloid morphogenesis. Using complementary genetic and pharmacological approaches, we demonstrate that elevated nuclear YAP activity impairs symmetry breaking and inhibits gastruloid elongation, whereas YAP inhibition enhances axial elongation compared with control conditions. Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) further reveals that YAP activation disrupts lineage segregation and compromises the emergence of distinct anterior and posterior cell populations along the anterior-posterior axis. In contrast, YAP inhibition promotes clearer segregation of these domains and facilitates axial elongation. Together, these findings establish a role for YAP activity in coordinating symmetry breaking, axial elongation, and anterior-posterior organization during human gastruloid development.

supplemented_raw_records.title: Multi-scale hybrid correction of noisy long reads
supplemented_raw_records.abstract: Long-read sequencing offers superior genome resolution but is hindered by error rates of 1-15%. Existing correction methods often struggle to suppress sequencing errors without removing genuine biological variation, leading to over-correction. DADEC addresses this trade-off through a confidence-ordered framework comprising stringent de Bruijn graph (DBG) correction, haplotype-aware short-read alignment refinement, and permissive DBG recovery. Across seven simulated and three real datasets, DADEC achieved the lowest mismatch and indel rates in most benchmark settings while maintaining high haplotype coverage. DADEC also improved assembly contiguity and strain-level metagenomic classification. On an independently simulated  Arabidopsis thaliana  dataset with ground truth, DADEC reduced correction-event false discovery and false negative rates by 38.9% and 40.2%, respectively, compared with the next-best method. DADEC therefore provides an accurate hybrid correction strategy for noisy long reads while reducing over-correction and maintaining haplotype representation.

supplemented_raw_records.title: ShapeUpLMD: Automated spatial optimization of laser microdissection for tissue sampling
supplemented_raw_records.abstract: Laser microdissection (LMD) enables enrichment of defined cellular populations from heterogeneous tissues but lacks standardized approaches for generating optimized regions of interest (ROIs) for scalable spatial multi-omic workflows. We developed ShapeUpLMD, an open-source tool that optimizes digitally annotated ROIs for automated spatial LMD workflows. Uterine serous carcinoma tumor ( n = 11) tissue sections were pathologist-annotated, and tumor-specific HALO classifier-generated ROIs were refined by ShapeUpLMD and collected using a Leica LMD7. Classifier-estimated tumor ROIs increased effective tumor purity by 86 ± 6% relative to whole tissue while maintaining strong concordance between predicted and collected regions (accuracy = 0.90 ± 0.05). Data-independent acquisition mass spectrometry quantified upwards of 6,500 proteins, revealing regionally coherent clustering and patterns consistent with tumor and non-tumor cell admixture. ShapeUpLMD provides an automated, scalable framework linking digital pathology with high-fidelity LMD for standardized spatial multi-omic profiling. ShapeUpLMD is freely available at https://github.com/GYNCOE/ShapeUpLMD.

supplemented_raw_records.title: Ion regulatory mechanisms supporting hypersaline tolerance in the coastal rock pool mosquito Aedes togoi
supplemented_raw_records.abstract: The coastal rock pool mosquito,  Aedes togoi,  is a remarkable example of a saline-tolerant mosquito. While most mosquitoes are obligate freshwater breeders,  Ae. togoi  larvae and pupae inhabit coastal rock pools that span freshwater to hypersaline conditions. We explore the ability of  Ae. togoi  larvae to tolerate hypersaline conditions by profiling the salt gland, an ion regulatory nexus within an anatomically unique, elaborated anal canal. We present a  de-novo  chromosome-scale genome assembly for  Ae. togoi , highlighting its relatively small genome size and differences in chromosomal structure as compared to other  Aedine  mosquitoes. We detail repeat content and curate key multi-gene families encoding ion-transport proteins enriched in the larval salt gland, building a model of the machinery that likely facilitates hyperosmotic urine formation. Our work provides insights into molecular and anatomical adaptations that underpin the ability of mosquitoes and other insects to thrive in hypersaline rock pools and other dynamic environments.

supplemented_raw_records.title: Highly twinned cobalt selenide with abundant selenium vacancies for efficient nitrogen reduction reaction
supplemented_raw_records.abstract: Electrocatalytic nitrogen reduction reaction (NRR) offers a promising approach to produce ammonia (NH 3 ) under ambient conditions. However, the ammonia yield rate and Faradaic efficiency were still limited by the chemical inertness of nitrogen. Here, we report the introduction of Se vacancies in CoSe nanorods via an ion-exchange method. Se vacancies can improve the NRR activities by the lending of N 2  activation. As a result, the ammonia yield rate reached as high as 106.7 μg h -1  mg -1  with a Faradaic efficiency of 21.2% at -0.3 V (vs. RHE). More importantly, the ammonia is directly derived from nitrogen, which was demonstrated by the isotopic experiments using  15 N 2  as a nitrogen source. This work not only provides a strategy for creating Se vacancies but also offers an important pathway for the development of efficient catalysts for the NRR.

supplemented_raw_records.title: Chromatin compartment shifting is recurrent and associated with epigenetic reprogramming in prostate cancer
supplemented_raw_records.abstract: Three-dimensional chromatin organization shapes gene regulation by partitioning the genome into transcriptionally active and inactive compartments, with implications for prostate carcinogenesis. We integrated Hi-C, ATAC-seq, and transcriptomic data from 18 clinical samples representing benign prostatic hyperplasia, primary prostate cancer (PC), and castration-resistant prostate cancer (CRPC). Using a computational framework accounting for copy number variation and tumor purity, we characterized A/B chromatin compartment organization in aneuploid tumors. We identified recurrent shifts from inactive B to active A compartments in both PC and CRPC, indicating shared chromatin reorganization across disease stages. These regions were enriched for prostate cancer-associated gene expression, including the biomarker  PCA3 , active epigenetic marks, and accessible chromatin bound by prostate lineage transcription factors, including AR, FOXA1, and HOXB13. These findings link higher-order chromatin organization to transcriptional and epigenetic rewiring, highlighting compartment shifts as a recurring feature of prostate carcinogenesis.

supplemented_raw_records.title: Receptor-guided phage cocktails constrain Acinetobacter baumannii resistance and improve therapy
supplemented_raw_records.abstract: The rise of multidrug-resistant (MDR) bacteria threatens global health by eroding the efficacy of existing antibiotics, underscoring the urgency of alternative therapies like phage therapy. Although bacteriophages are promising owing to their abundance, diversity, and potent bactericidal activity, their therapeutic durability is compromised by the rapid emergence of phage resistance. Here, we explore receptor complementarity as a proof-of-concept rational strategy to overcome this bottleneck. This study demonstrates that phage resistance imposes substantial fitness costs while still permitting bacterial survival under phage pressure. By isolating phages with distinct receptor dependencies, we constructed receptor-diverse phage cocktails that decreased the frequency of phage resistance. Notably, these receptor-informed cocktails suppressed phage resistance  in vitro  and yielded improved prophylactic and therapeutic efficacy in the  Galleria mellonella  preclinical  in vivo  model. Collectively, this work offers preclinical proof-of-concept for receptor-guided cocktail design to enhance the performance of phage-based interventions against MDR pathogens.

supplemented_raw_records.title: A synNotch-based morphogen detection system reveals sFRP2 enhances Wnt3a signaling
supplemented_raw_records.abstract: Morphogen gradients provide essential positional information during tissue development, yet the extracellular mechanisms that regulate morphogen transport remain elusive. Here, we introduce a mechanosensitive detection system based on synthetic Notch (synNotch) receptors that selectively detect surface-bound morphogens. Applying this platform to Wnt signaling, we demonstrate that secreted Frizzled-related protein 2 (sFRP2) promotes the recruitment of Wnt3a to the cell surface via heparan sulfate proteoglycans, enabling robust activation of canonical Wnt/β-catenin signaling. Notably, sFRP2 extends the effective signaling range of Wnt3a under ligand-limiting conditions. In intestinal organoid cultures, sFRP2 enhances Wnt3a-driven growth and induces high-Wnt morphological states even at low Wnt3a concentrations. These findings identify sFRP2 as an extracellular carrier that stabilizes surface-bound Wnt3a and regulates both the strength and spatial range of Wnt signaling. Broadly, this work demonstrates the utility of synNotch mechano-sensing for dissecting extracellular morphogen dynamics and highlights the potential of morphogen carrier proteins to optimize organoid culture.

supplemented_raw_records.title: Estrogen loss activates inflammatory memory T-cells associated with postpartum mood symptoms and hippocampal signaling changes
supplemented_raw_records.abstract: The rapid decline in estrogen (E 2 ) after childbirth is associated with postpartum anxiety and depression. We previously identified a murine pathway in which E 2 loss increases IL-7 and IL-15, activating inflammatory memory T-cells (T M ). Here, we investigated whether this pathway is activated in humans by E 2 loss using a longitudinal observational study design of women during late pregnancy and approximately seven weeks postpartum. E 2 decline was associated with FasL loss, increased IL-7 and IL-15, altered dendritic-cell phenotype, and activation of TNFα- and IL-17A-producing T M , which strongly correlated with Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale scores. To investigate the mechanism, we used a murine E 2 -withdrawal model. E 2 loss induced anxiety-like behavior, impaired short-term memory, neurovascular changes, and T M activation. T-cell-specific ablation of IL-15 receptor prevented inflammatory T M activation and behavioral abnormalities despite persistent neurovascular changes, identifying an IL-15-dependent endocrine-immune pathway associated with postpartum mood symptoms.

supplemented_raw_records.title: Functional characterization of the pheromone receptor OR67d within the genus Drosophila
supplemented_raw_records.abstract: Insects rely on chemosensory cues to mediate essential behaviors, including mate recognition. In  Drosophila melanogaster , the odorant receptor OR67d detects the male-specific pheromone  cis -vaccenyl acetate (cVA), initiating diverse behavioral responses. However, the evolutionary conservation and functional tuning of OR67d receptors across  Drosophila  species remain largely unexplored. Here, we characterize OR67d receptors from nine  Drosophila  species using phylogenetic analysis, transgenic expression, and electrophysiology. While most orthologs retained sensitivity to cVA, some exhibited broader tuning, responding to structurally similar acetates. Notably,  D. bipectinata  and  D. navojoa  responded to cVA despite not producing it, raising the possibility that cVA detection has been maintained independently of endogenous production, possibly as a heterospecific cue. Structural modeling revealed overall high sequence conservation yet identified variable regions within the putative binding pocket potentially underlying differences in ligand selectivity. These findings contribute to our understanding of pheromone receptor evolution and how chemical communication systems diversify across  Drosophila  species.

supplemented_raw_records.title: Intra-tissular targeting of subcutaneous adipose progenitors by adipocyte-derived mitochondria transfer
supplemented_raw_records.abstract: Adipocytes are active mitochondria donors in vivo , through production of extracellular vesicles. We investigated specific properties of 3T3-L1 adipocyte mitochondria and their impact when transferred to mouse adipose progenitors in primary culture. We show that adipocytes display fragmented mitochondria morphology and low membrane potential compared to fibroblast-like 3T3-L1 preadipocytes. They externalize mitochondria in the form of extracellular vesicles when acutely stimulated with autophagy inhibitors or β-adrenergic agonists. Transfer of adipose mitochondria to mouse progenitors in primary culture occurred with high frequency, and did not impact adipose conversion within the bulk stroma-vascular cell fraction. We report that mitochondria transfer upregulates ECM-related gene expression, selectively in subcutaneous but not visceral progenitors, associated with a specific gene subset enriched in a recently defined "Structural Wnt-regulated Adipose Tissue" cell subtype (SWAT). We suggest that intra-tissular adipose mitochondria transfer in subcutaneous fat has potential to reprogram progenitor subtypes to maintain stem cell reservoir.

supplemented_raw_records.title: When artificial intelligence falls short: Multimodal analysis improves head and neck lymphoma classification
authors: Cinthia Veronica Bardález López de Cáceres
supplemented_raw_records.abstract: Artificial intelligence is increasingly applied in digital pathology, yet its generalizability in routine diagnostic settings remains challenging. We developed a multimodal framework for classifying head and neck lymphoid lesions using 610 cases from ten institutions. UNI was used for histological feature extraction, while CellViT++ enabled nuclear segmentation and quantitative morphometry, subsequently integrated with clinicopathological variables. The UNI-based model showed limited generalization (accuracy of 0.66, F1 score of 0.65, and Area Under the Receiver Operating Characteristic curve (AUROC) of 0.66), whereas multimodal integration substantially improved internal performance (accuracy of 0.91, F1 score of 0.91, and AUROC of 0.87) and maintained performance across two external cohorts (accuracy of 0.84 and 0.79 and AUROC of 0.84 and 0.80). Class-stratified SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis revealed distinct feature attribution patterns across diagnostic groups, with nuclear morphometric features contributing prominently to model predictions. Morphology alone imposes a clear performance ceiling in head and neck lymphomas. Multimodal integration provides a more reliable and clinically relevant approach, supporting diagnostic triage in routine practice.

supplemented_raw_records.title: Biogeography and monsoon-associated climatic trait evolution in true frogs Rana
supplemented_raw_records.abstract: Climatic variation across latitude shapes lineage diversification and niche evolution. We integrated multilocus and genome-wide SNPs, morphological characters, historical biogeography, and phylogenetic comparative analyses for 391 sampled individuals representing 21 recognised  Rana  species across the Palearctic. Time-calibrated total-evidence analyses resolved three major stem lineages originating in the Early Miocene, 22.00 Mya, followed by radiations across East Asia and the central Palearctic. Biogeographic reconstruction supported a northward expansion of the  Rana amurensis  lineage into Siberia, c. 7.67 Mya, coinciding with relatively warm Arctic conditions. Climate-latitude relationships were weak across Ranidae, but stronger and lineage-dependent in Eastern Palearctic  Rana , particularly in relation to monsoon-related climatic variables. Across lineages, broad latitudinal ranges evolved independently in Eurasian  Pelophylax ridibundus ,  R. amurensis ,  R. dybowskii , and  R. temporaria  (c. 30.00 Mya), with additional origins in Nearctic  Lithobates catesbeianus  and  L. sylvaticus  (c. 12.00 Mya). This homoplasy highlights the influence of climatic transitions on ranid diversification.

supplemented_raw_records.title: Hippocampal theta aligns to paw movements during a forelimb-dominated sensorimotor behavior
supplemented_raw_records.abstract: Hippocampal theta oscillations organize neural activity to support navigation, memory, and sensorimotor integration. Theta is also modulated by running speed, and this relationship may stabilize neural representations of space. Furthermore, theta alignment to task-relevant movements suggests its role in sensorimotor integration. Here, theta was examined during string pulling to determine if established relationships between theta and movement extend to bimanual pulling behaviors. Five Sprague-Dawley rats performed the task and were rewarded for pulling a predefined length of string. Analysis of local-field activity in dorsal CA1 revealed that the established positive relationship between theta frequency, speed, and acceleration during running was absent or reversed during pulling. Further, theta power and phase locking peaked during the paw's downward push. Since phase locking is associated with sensorimotor gating, theta phase alignment during the push could reflect gating of inputs relevant for reaching the reward.

supplemented_raw_records.title: Site-comprehensive phosphorylation dismantles a disordered interaction hub to drive Cdc25C activation
supplemented_raw_records.abstract: The Cdk1 activator Cdc25C contains a long intrinsically disordered regulatory region (IDR) that mediates the IDR-catalytic domain interaction, substrate recruitment via interaction with cyclin B, self-association, and heterotypic interactions with numerous partners. While site-comprehensive phosphorylation across the IDR dramatically activates Cdc25C at M-phase onset, prior site-specific phosphorylation produces only modest activation. Here, we show that the IDR functions as a phosphorylation-responsive interaction hub whose interaction state determines whether Cdc25C remains restrained or transitions to an active state. Before M-phase entry, site-specific phosphorylation selectively rewires the IDR-mediated interaction network, promoting cyclin B recruitment to modestly activate Cdc25C. At M-phase entry, site-comprehensive phosphorylation globally dismantles all four classes of IDR-mediated interactions to enable robust Cdc25C activation. These findings illustrate how site-comprehensive phosphorylation of long IDRs can function as a decisive biochemical switch and provide a mechanistic framework for understanding the biphasic regulation of Cdc25C activity during M-phase induction.

supplemented_raw_records.title: Integrative analysis of pooled CRISPR screens provide functional insights into AD GWAS risk genes
supplemented_raw_records.abstract: Microglia pathways such as lipid transport and metabolism, phagocytosis, and lysosomal function are implicated Alzheimer's disease (AD) pathology, but the mechanisms underlying these pathways remain poorly understood. To map these pathways, custom CRISPR activation and interference (CRISPRa/i) libraries were constructed targeting 203 microglial and genome-wide association study (GWAS)-associated risk genes. Pooled CRISPRa/i screens in THP-1 cells identified core functional regulators of lipid metabolism and lysosomal function, a subset of which were validated in primary macrophages. We also captured transcriptomic changes caused by these genes by performing Perturb-seq in primary macrophages. Through non-negative matrix factorization, we identified five gene programs altered by our perturbation library. We then used an integrative analysis of functional screen data with Perturb-seq data that enabled us to uncover novel functions and genetic relationships between perturbations. This multidimensional resource links genetic perturbations to phenotypes and transcriptional programs, establishing a scalable framework for systematic gene discovery in neurodegeneration and beyond.

supplemented_raw_records.title: Determinants of progression of filarial lymphedema in a clinic-based cohort: Implications for global elimination
supplemented_raw_records.abstract: Lymphatic filariasis remains a leading cause of chronic, debilitating lymphedema. Global health initiatives emphasize morbidity management and disability prevention (MMDP) through routine self-care to limit disease progression. To evaluate the long-term clinical trajectory of this condition, we objectively quantified limb volume changes and their determinants in a retrospective cohort of 110 adult patients with filarial lower limb lymphedema in Puducherry, India, over a median follow-up of nine years. Our analysis revealed that disease stability is highly attainable, with nearly half (46.4%) of the cohort exhibiting no volumetric progression. While recurrent adenolymphangitis episodes and baseline hypertension correlated with progression severity, multivariable regression identified strict adherence to home-based MMDP self-care practices as the primary independent predictor of halted or reduced limb volume change. These findings demonstrate that sustained behavioral adherence to simple self-care interventions can effectively mitigate chronic lymphedema. Integrating robust patient education and long-term adherence support into routine clinical care is therefore paramount within the global elimination program to prevent further disability in affected populations worldwide.

supplemented_raw_records.title: Centrosome depletion reprograms RNA splicing to promote neuroblastoma differentiation through SR factor dephosphorylation
supplemented_raw_records.abstract: Centrosomes are key regulators of cell division and may also contribute to cell fate determination. By combining immunoprecipitation with spatial immunofluorescence in neuroblastoma stem cells, we found that U2 and U5 small nuclear RNAs (snRNAs) preferentially associate with centrosomal subdistal appendages (sDAPs), mirroring the localization of the SR splicing factor SRSF2.
