Retinoic acid (RA)-induced neuronal differentiation was accompanied by coordinated changes in centrosome expression and pre-mRNA splicing. Notably, PLK4 inhibition-induced centriolar loss prior to RA treatment enhanced neuronal maturation. Centrosome depletion was further associated with increased intron retention and dephosphorylation of SR splicing factors, including SRSF2, at the centrosome. Analysis of a retained intron in the centrosome-associated WDR13 transcript identified two 3′ splice acceptor sites whose usage was reduced following centrosome depletion. Together, these findings reveal that centrosome loss reprograms RNA splicing to promote neuroblastoma differentiation, revealing a potential strategy for programmable control of cell fate.

supplemented_raw_records.title: Anodic molybdenum-oxide nanofilms for antibacterial application
supplemented_raw_records.abstract: Antibacterial coatings, passive and active, are critical for biomedical applications, and the present work offers original solutions by combining these two strategies. An array of MoO   x   -NbO   x   mixed-oxide  nano-needles  having 68 at.% Mo was synthesized by anodizing a sputter-deposited Al/Mo-Nb-alloy bilayer. The upper Al layer was first transformed into a porous anodic alumina (PAA) film, which guided the anodizing of the alloy and was finally selectively dissolved. Alternatively, a  nano-smooth  anodic MoO   x   -NbO   x   film having 87 at.% Mo was synthesized similarly, finishing with the dissolution of both the PAA and the oxide inside the pores. The films were tested against G-negative  E .  coli  and G-positive  S .  aureus  bacteria. The results suggest that the nano-needle array causes a strong, harmful synergetic impact on the bacteria, combining the anti-adhesive (passive) and contact-killing or ion-releasing (active) effects, while the nano-smooth film is more practical thanks to its robust, multitouchable, and washable surface.

supplemented_raw_records.title: Who will import hydrogen in 2050? Global assessment with China and U.S. case studies
supplemented_raw_records.abstract: This study assesses the global hydrogen import requirements in 2050 by analyzing renewable hydrogen production potential in prospective import-oriented countries. Candidate importers are identified using GIS-based renewable energy potentials and projected 2050 primary energy demand. Two approaches are applied: (1) a meta-analysis of published hydrogen demand and production potential estimates, and (2) detailed regional analyses for the United States and China. The literature-based analysis indicates regionally concentrated imports of 128-1,255 TWh, with median and mean estimates of 458 and 438 TWh. Germany, Italy, and the Netherlands emerge as likely net importers, while several Asian countries have sufficient renewable resources to cover projected demand. The United States is well positioned to meet its demand domestically, whereas eastern China could require an additional 0-550 TWh of imports, depending on the share met internationally. Overall, import requirements depend on renewable resource distribution, energy demand, alternative hydrogen production pathways, and infrastructure constraints.

supplemented_raw_records.title: Astrocytes contribute to long-chain polyunsaturated fatty acid metabolism affecting microglia in fragile X syndrome
supplemented_raw_records.abstract: Polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs) influence membrane structure and function, energy metabolism, inflammation, and the ability to regulate microglial activity. We show involvement of astrocytes in long-chain PUFA metabolism in human induced pluripotent stem cell (hiPSC)-derived astrocytes with fragile X syndrome (FXS). FXS astrocytes secreted more n-6 docosapentaenoic acid (n-6 DPA) and displayed a higher n-3 DPA to docosahexaenoic acid (DHA) ratio in medium than controls, consistent with an altered n-6 to n-3 PUFA balance in plasma from the FXS mouse. The FXS-specific increase in n-6 DPA secretion was abolished by treatment with all- trans retinoic acid (ATRA), which affected gene expression in astrocyte subpopulations and modulated secreted triacylglycerol species. Microglial exposure to n-6 DPA stimulated expression of brain-derived neurotrophic factor ( BDNF ), which also tended to increase in microglia with reduced inflammatory marker expression when cultured in medium from ATRA-treated astrocytes. The results indicate that astrocyte-mediated n-6 DPA regulates the trophic functions of microglia in FXS.

supplemented_raw_records.title: A deep learning model for flood forecasting based on dynamic lag encoding and multi-head attention
supplemented_raw_records.abstract: Conventional flood forecasting models often struggle to effectively capture the time-lag characteristics of rainfall-runoff responses within a basin, and their decision-making processes generally lack interpretability. This study used 19 years (1979-1997) of multi-station rainfall and outlet discharge data from the Hydrological Yearbook of the Yellow River Basin, and selected 53 representative flood events from the Huangfuchuan Basin for model development and evaluation. A deep learning flood forecasting model (D-TMA-LSTM) was developed by integrating dynamic lag encoding with a multi-head attention mechanism. The results show that D-TMA-LSTM outperformed the original LSTM and D-LSTM across forecast lead times from t+1 to t+6. At t+1, NSE, KGE, and R 2  values were 0.959, 0.934, and 0.964, respectively, while RMSE decreased by 31.74%. The model also maintained stable performance at t+6, providing an effective framework for flood forecasting in basins with complex rainfall-runoff lag responses.

supplemented_raw_records.title: Effects of chronic sucrose consumption on behavior, metabolism, and dopaminergic markers in an ADHD model
supplemented_raw_records.abstract: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) involves dopaminergic dysfunction, and excessive sugar intake has been proposed to aggravate ADHD-related traits through mesolimbic reward pathways. We gave male spontaneously hypertensive rats (SHRs), a model of ADHD, and their Wistar Kyoto (WKY) controls intermittent access to 10% sucrose for 21 days and assessed behavior, metabolism, and frontostriatal dopaminergic markers. SHRs consumed more sucrose than WKY rats on the first day of access, consistent with novelty seeking. Sucrose impaired open field habituation in both strains and recognition memory in WKY rats, and selectively increased anxiety-like behavior in the open field in SHRs. Sucrose also elevated blood glucose in both strains and triglycerides and total cholesterol in SHRs, whereas dopamine D2 receptor and dopamine transporter expression remained largely unchanged. Thus, genetic background shapes the emotional, cognitive, and metabolic responses to dietary sugar, and ADHD-like phenotypes may carry a heightened metabolic vulnerability.

supplemented_raw_records.title: Space-number association in zebrafish
supplemented_raw_records.abstract: Spatial-numerical associations reflect the tendency to map small numerosities to the left and larger numerosities to the right. Although widely documented in humans and some non-human species, its presence in teleost fish has remained unclear. Here, we investigated whether zebrafish exhibit a spatial-numerical association by presenting fish with a left-right numerical discrimination task in a controlled behavioral assay. Zebrafish exhibited systematic magnitude-dependent spatial choices, showing a significant spatial shift toward the left for smaller relative to larger numerosities across experimental conditions. These results provide evidence for a number-space association in zebrafish and suggest that number-space mapping may extend to basal vertebrate lineages. This highlights zebrafish as a promising model for investigating the neurobiological mechanisms underlying number-space associations.

supplemented_raw_records.title: Systematic CRISPR screens decode regulators of primary human pathogenic Th17 cell differentiation and activation
supplemented_raw_records.abstract: Summary: T-helper 17 (Th17) cells mediate host defense against bacterial and fungal pathogens at mucosal and skin interfaces. However, they are also involved in the pathogenesis of diverse autoimmune and inflammatory diseases. To accelerate candidate discovery in the pathogenic Th17 pathway, we have customized druggable CRISPR activation (CRISPRa) and interference (CRISPRi) sgRNA libraries. With an optimized Th17 differentiation protocol, we performed customized CRISPRa and CRISPRi screens in human peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) to identify potential regulators controlling the function of pathogenic Th17 cells. Coupled with next-generation sequencing, our screens identified previously reported and undiscovered genes involved in pathogenic Th17 cell differentiation and activation. Among them, the regulatory roles of heme oxygenase 1 and CD28 were verified by sgRNA-based and small-molecule inhibitor-based functional experiments in vitro . Our study provided a useful resource for mapping key genes of pathogenic Th17 cell function and potential immunotherapy targets for treating Th17-related immune disorders.

supplemented_raw_records.title: Survival and laryngeal preservation with neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy in hypopharyngeal carcinoma: A multicenter study
supplemented_raw_records.abstract: Optimal neoadjuvant therapy for resectable locally advanced hypopharyngeal carcinoma (LAHC) remains clinically important. In this multicenter retrospective cohort of 517 patients, taxane-platinum-fluorouracil (TPF), TPF plus targeted therapy, and taxane-platinum (TP) plus immunotherapy were compared before surgery-based multimodal therapy or radical (chemo) radiotherapy. TP plus immunotherapy achieved superior overall survival (hazard ratio [HR] 0.62), progression-free survival (HR 0.65), and laryngectomy-free survival (HR 0.59), with the highest pathologic complete response (25.4%) and laryngeal preservation rate (83.7%). Surgery-based multimodal therapy, lymph node metastasis, and P16 negativity further stratified survival, response, and resistance. These findings suggest that neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy may improve survival and laryngeal preservation in resectable LAHC, supporting prospective evaluation of immunotherapy-containing induction strategies.

supplemented_raw_records.title: Non-autonomous PMK-1/p38 MAPK signaling ensures homeostatic downregulation of germline stem cell proliferation in C. elegans
supplemented_raw_records.abstract: Stem cell underproliferation leads to tissue loss, while overproliferation can induce tumorigenesis. Stem and progenitor proliferation rates are therefore coupled to the needs for differentiated cells in the tissues they maintain, yet these homeostatic mechanisms remain poorly characterized. Here, we used the C. elegans hermaphrodite reproductive system to understand how germline stem cell (GSC) proliferation is linked to sperm availability and oocyte usage. We designed a forward genetic screening strategy to identify germline homeostasis-defective ( ghd ) mutants that grow benign, differentiated germline tumors akin to hamartomas. We provide evidence that the TIR-1/sterile alpha and TIR-motif containing 1 (SARM1) metabolic sensor works together with the NIPI-3/TRIB1 pseudokinase to activate a canonical PMK-1/p38 mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) signaling cascade in the somatic gonadal sheath, where it shuts down the oncogenic extracellular signal-regulated kinase MPK-1/ERK to cell non-autonomously couple GSC proliferation with oocyte needs. Similar PMK-1/p38-dependent inter-tissue signaling modules could underlie stem cell homeostasis in other systems and prevent differentiated tumors.

supplemented_raw_records.title: Urbanization does not affect how wolves respond to a simulated dog encounter
Composition-driven electronic-state engineering of refractory Zr1-xHfxN for broadband space thermal control
supplemented_raw_records.abstract: Refractory broadband reflectors are desirable for reducing radiative heat loads in long-duration space cryogenic systems. Here, composition-dependent radiative regulation in rocksalt Zr 1-x Hf x N is investigated using first-principles calculations combined with an experimentally calibrated intraband Drude correction. Hf substitution continuously transfers near-Fermi metal-d orbital weight from Zr-4d to Hf-5d states while producing non-monotonic changes in the electronic and dielectric responses. These effects generate a broadband optical optimum at Zr 0.25 Hf 0.75 N, which exhibits an AM0-weighted solar reflectance of 85.80%, a solar absorptance of 0.1420, and a Planck-weighted infrared emittance of 0.0448 at 300 K that remains nearly unchanged from 300 to 400 K. The coincident solar and infrared optima demonstrate that composition engineering can simultaneously suppress solar absorption and thermal-infrared emission, providing a design route for refractory reflective surfaces for space cryogenic thermal management.

supplemented_raw_records.title: Bundled AI supported automated breast ultrasound versus handheld ultrasound in organized screening in China
supplemented_raw_records.abstract: Evidence for AI-supported ultrasound screening programs remains limited. We compared a bundled AI-supported automated breast ultrasound (ABUS) workflow with handheld ultrasound (HHUS) in a government-organized screening program. Adjusted risk ratios accounted for baseline imbalance, and standardized cancer detection rate (CDR) accounted for differential biopsy completion. ABUS reduced recall (12.1% vs. 29.9%; adjusted RR 0.45 [95% CI 0.42-0.48]) and biopsy recall (0.99% vs. 2.19%; adjusted RR 0.50 [0.39-0.64]), while increasing biopsy positive predictive value (PPV; 62.1% vs. 20.0%; adjusted RR 2.46 [1.34-4.52]). Observed CDR was higher but not statistically significant (3.08 vs. 1.22 per 1000; adjusted rate ratios 1.90 [0.94-3.86]). Early-stage proportion was higher with ABUS but not statistically significant (84.8% vs. 50.0%; adjusted RR 1.64 [0.71-3.80]). The bundled ABUS pathway was associated with substantially lower recall and higher biopsy PPV. Findings for cancer detection and stage distribution were exploratory because of differential biopsy completion and the small number of cancers.

supplemented_raw_records.title: Pore suppression in adjustable ring-mode laser lap welding of dissimilar-thickness 1060 aluminum alloy
supplemented_raw_records.abstract: Adjustable ring-mode (ARM) laser welding mitigates thermal asymmetry and porosity in dissimilar-thickness aluminum lap joints for power batteries. A multi-physics thermal-fluid model with combined volumetric heat source simulates 1.5 + 1 mm 1060 alloy at 100 mm/s under four power cases, validated within 14.29% error. Keyhole volume  3  causes unstable penetration and vapor trapping; >0.59 mm 3 , stable penetration ≥0.25 mm 3  keeps open vapor channels and reduces porosity. Recoil-pressure spatial standard deviation (SSD) evolution, not magnitude, controls pore susceptibility: case 3 holds SSD = 151.60 Pa (70-90 ms, maintain-then-smooth trend, 2.333% porosity), while case 2 rapidly falls to 106.06 Pa with 0.504 mm 3  keyhole volume and 4.251% porosity. Optimal ring-core power ratio: 0.8-1.2. Combined volume threshold and SSD evolution clarify pore suppression and guide power battery joining optimization.

supplemented_raw_records.title: Allopatric speciation of Oroperipatus velvet worms driven by Andean orogenesis and paleoclimate
supplemented_raw_records.abstract: The role of Andean orogeny in the diversification of ancient, low-vagility terrestrial invertebrates remains poorly understood. Herein, we examined Andean onychophorans ( Oroperipatus ) to evaluate how climatic change and vicariant processes associated with Andean uplift influenced speciation and their disjunct distribution across the Americas. Morphological and molecular analyses of 13 species sampled across the taxon's range revealed strong concordance between geography and phylogenetic structure, identifying two main lineages gathering eastern (Amazonian) and western (Pacific) Andean species, respectively. Divergence-time analyses suggest that these two lineages predate major Andean uplift and were likely shaped by paleoclimatic and vegetational changes. Later diversification was probably driven by climatic, ecological, and vicariant processes linked to the diachronous rise of the Andes. Close relationship among Ecuadorian, Galápagos, and Mexican species suggests stepwise dispersal via transient Pacific islands or independent Miocene-Pliocene overwater dispersal from Ecuador. Ten new species are described, increasing known  Oroperipatus  diversity by ∼50%.

supplemented_raw_records.title: Van der Waals heterojunctions: An emerging pathway toward high-performance perovskite solar cells
supplemented_raw_records.abstract: Metal halide perovskite solar cells (PSCs) have achieved impressive power conversion efficiencies, yet poorly controlled crystallization, interfacial recombination, ion migration, and operational instability continue to impede further progress. Van der Waals heterojunctions (vdWHs) from two-dimensional materials provide a distinctive interface engineering platform. Their atomically smooth surfaces, weak interlayer coupling, high tolerance to lattice mismatch, and tunable electronic structures enable simultaneous structural and electronic regulation. This review examines the roles of vdWHs in PSCs through the lens of synergistic regulation at multifunctional interfaces. We first contrast conventional heterojunctions with vdWHs to clarify their unique interfacial features, and then trace how interfacial structure and coupling regulate perovskite crystallization while simultaneously governing band alignment, carrier transport, and degradation pathways under operating conditions. Finally, persistent challenges related to mechanistic understanding, interfacial diagnostics, operando studies, and scalable manufacturing are outlined to guide the development of efficient, durable, and manufacturable perovskite photovoltaics.

supplemented_raw_records.title: Guanidinium-driven fluorescence detection of microcystins using carbon dot embedded silica nanoparticles
supplemented_raw_records.abstract: Detection of microcystins in environmental waters is constrained by complex analytical methods and the cost of whole-toxin-based imprinting techniques. Herein, we report a carbon-dot-embedded silica molecularly imprinted polymer (CDSiMIP) nanosensor prepared using L-arginine as a surrogate fragment template. The Arg-CDSiMIP nanosensor showed preferential fluorescence responses toward guanidyl-bearing microcystins, achieving detection limits of 33 ng L -1  for microcystin-LR (0-450 ng L -1 ) and 13 ng L -1  for microcystin-RR (0-400 ng L -1 ) with an interaction/response time of 15 min. Substantial microcystin-LR-induced quenching was maintained over a pH range of 6.0-10.0, whereas environmental interferents, free amino acids, and a photosynthetic pigment extract produced comparatively lower responses. In spiked lake water, fluorescence-based recoveries were 105%-117% (relative standard deviation ≤1.5%), with concentration estimates generally comparable to those obtained by independent mass spectrometric measurements. These findings establish the fragment-imprinted CDSiMIP nanosensor as a sensitive, rapid optical screening platform for detecting microcystins in environmental water.

supplemented_raw_records.title: AI optimized fertilization and irrigation improve wheat yield and quality in semi-arid calcareous soils
supplemented_raw_records.abstract: Traditional wheat farming in calcareous, low-organic-carbon, semi-arid environments relies on blanket fertilization and calendar-based irrigation, causing low nitrogen use efficiency and poor grain quality. We compared traditional practice with an AI-optimized system using soil test-based fertilization and tensiometer-guided irrigation for winter wheat in Khuzestan, Iran. The AI system reduced water use by 12.5% and nitrogen fertilizer by 28% while increasing grain yield by 8.5%. Water productivity improved by 24%, nitrogen use efficiency rose from 43% to 72%, grain protein increased by 13%, zinc by 43%, and iron by 33%. Soil organic carbon increased from 0.42% to 0.48%, microbial biomass carbon increased by 68%, and net greenhouse gas emissions fell by 43%. These findings show that simple, affordable AI tools can support sustainable intensification in semi-arid wheat systems.

supplemented_raw_records.title: RNF5/185 deficiency reveals a distinct compensatory role for AMFR in mutant CFTR ERAD
supplemented_raw_records.abstract: Abnormal proteins in the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) are eliminated by ER-associated degradation (ERAD), a quality-control network governed by multiple ubiquitin E3 ligases. We examined how mammalian ERAD maintains degradation capacity when a major E3 ligase pathway is impaired. Here, we identified AMFR as a compensatory factor for mutant cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator (CFTR) degradation in cells lacking RNF5 and RNF185 (RNF5/185). RNF5/185 double-knockout cells showed increased AMFR protein abundance and reduced AMFR turnover, while AMFR mRNA exhibited an upward trend. AMFR depletion had a relatively limited effect on CFTR degradation in WT cells but markedly impaired degradation in RNF5/185-deficient cells. By contrast, several other ER-associated E3 ligases, including the AMFR homolog SYVN1, did not show a comparable compensatory effect. These findings indicate that AMFR-dependent ERAD functionally compensates for RNF5/185 deficiency and suggest that mammalian ERAD is an adaptable proteostasis network in which E3 ligase contributions shift with cellular context.

supplemented_raw_records.title: Aging drives region specific metabolic changes in gut muscularis macrophages
supplemented_raw_records.abstract: Muscularis macrophages (MMs) are tissue-resident macrophages embedded in the gut muscle layer that regulate neuromuscular function. We show that aging causes metabolic remodeling of select small intestine (SI) MM subpopulations that share homeostatic features with microglia. These MMs, which are characterized by lipid droplet accumulation, show increased glycolytic and lipid-handling features, mitochondrial stress, increased lysosomal content, elevated inflammatory gene expression, and reduced phagocytic activity. Unlike SI, colon MMs are relatively resistant to this lipid-accumulating phenotype. Together, these findings show that MM metabolic aging in the gut is specific to region and subset and suggest that local intestinal environments and MM heterogeneity shape macrophage vulnerability during aging.

supplemented_raw_records.title: Metabolic profiling of brain and cerebrospinal fluid in cerebral malaria
supplemented_raw_records.abstract: Cerebral malaria (CM), a severe neurological complication of Plasmodium falciparum infection, is a common cause of pediatric mortality and long-term cognitive impairment in endemic regions. The mechanisms driving CM-associated coma and neuropathology are not fully understood. We performed untargeted metabolomic profiling of brain tissue from experimental cerebral malaria (ECM) mouse models and brain autopsy tissue and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) samples from children with CM and non-malarial coma (NMC). ECM brain samples exhibited significant metabolic alterations, including differences in energy metabolism and amino acids and elevated pipecolic and lactic acids. In contrast, CM and NMC brain metabolomes showed limited differences. CSF metabolomes from cohorts in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Malawi showed elevated glyceric acid in CM compared with NMC. Together, these findings highlight metabolic perturbations in CM across species and sample types and identify glyceric acid as a potential CSF biomarker.

supplemented_raw_records.title: Cell type-specific transcriptomic responses to progesterone and bazedoxifene prevent estradiol-driven proliferation in the human endometrium
supplemented_raw_records.abstract: Menopausal hormone therapy (MHT) combining estrogen with a progestogen protects the endometrium in non-hysterectomized women but increases breast cancer risk, prompting the search for progestogen-free alternatives. Selective estrogen receptor modulators (SERMs), such as bazedoxifene (BZA), offer a potential solution, yet their use for menopausal indications remains debated. MHT evaluations rely largely on mouse models or clinical measurements of endometrial thickness, providing limited mechanistic insight in human tissue. Here, we performed cell-type-specific transcriptomic profiling of patient-derived endometrial xenografts to compare how progesterone and BZA prevent estradiol-induced proliferation. Both treatments act through specific mechanisms: progesterone preserves half of the estradiol-dependent transcriptional response while inducing new programs, whereas BZA broadly abrogates estradiol-driven signaling in epithelial and stromal cells. We further identified cell-specific transcription factors and differential regulation of paracrine/autocrine networks. Overall, this study provides mechanistic and transcriptomic resources from human endometrium, with important implications for the development of improved MHT strategies.

supplemented_raw_records.title: Organelle distribution and protein translation defects in radial glia cells with mutations in Eml1
supplemented_raw_records.abstract: Cerebral cortical development is a finely regulated process, depending on key neuronal progenitors, giving rise to neurons that migrate to superficial regions in the brain. Disruptions can cause severe cortical malformations, associated with intellectual disability and epilepsy. Mutations in EML1/Eml1 , a microtubule-associated protein, lead to subcortical heterotopia in humans and mice. In mutant mouse brains, ectopic apical radial glia (aRG) progenitors were found outside the proliferative ventricular zone. The role of Eml1 in these cells remains unclear. Using proteomics and imaging approaches, we reveal that Eml1 regulates mitochondrial trafficking within aRG in vivo and influences mitochondrial and polysome distribution. Furthermore, Eml1 associates with translational machinery, and an overall downregulation of translation is observed in the Eml1 mutant aRG translatome. Paradoxically, an upregulation of translation-related mRNAs is also observed. These findings indicate that Eml1 regulates fundamental cellular mechanisms, including translation, crucial for aRG function and brain architecture.

supplemented_raw_records.title: CEBPB links human trophoblast dysfunction to NF-κB signaling and ferroptosis-related alterations in gestational diabetes
supplemented_raw_records.abstract: Summary: Gestational diabetes mellitus is associated with placental inflammation, oxidative stress, and trophoblast dysfunction. By integrating two placental transcriptomic datasets with experiments in high-glucose (HG)-treated human HTR-8/SVneo and Swan.71 trophoblast cells, we identified CCAAT/enhancer-binding protein β (CEBPB) as a candidate regulator of these changes. Mannitol controls, CEBPB depletion and overexpression, and Cell Counting Kit-8 , EdU, wound-healing, and Transwell assays linked CEBPB expression to impaired proliferation and migration. CEBPB overexpression increased NF-κB reporter activity, p65 and IκBα phosphorylation, inflammatory gene expression, lipid reactive oxygen species, intracellular Fe 2+ levels, and malondialdehyde levels. Pyrrolidine dithiocarbamate, p65 depletion, and ferrostatin-1 attenuated selected molecular or functional effects, and p65 depletion reduced CEBPB-associated lipid reactive oxygen species. These findings associate CEBPB with NF-κB-dependent inflammatory signaling and ferroptosis-related biochemical alterations during HG-induced trophoblast dysfunction, providing a framework for investigating placental injury in gestational diabetes, although it requires confirmation in clinical and in vivo models.

supplemented_raw_records.title: Dmcyp12c1 is required for eye development and retinal integrity during aging in Drosophila
supplemented_raw_records.abstract: Cytochrome P450 (CYP) enzymes regulate lipid metabolism and cellular homeostasis, yet their cell-type specific roles in the retina remain poorly understood. Using Drosophila melanogaster , we screened Cyp genes predicted to encode homologs of human CYP27A1 and identified Dmcyp12c1 as highly enriched in the retina and functionally critical in photoreceptors. Developmental photoreceptor-specific downregulation of Dmcyp12c1 gene reduces eye size and impairs pigmentation, while glial loss produces no phenotype. Adult-specific neuronal downregulation triggers progressive retinal degeneration characterized by ommatidial disorganization, retinal thinning, vacuole formation, and reduced retinal protein content. In contrast, glial downregulation produced no detectable phenotype. Surprisingly, degeneration occurred independently of cholesterol accumulation or lipid droplet formation, and dietary cholesterol supplementation does not reproduce retinal degeneration in control flies. Together, our findings identify the Dmcyp12c1 gene as a critical regulator of retinal integrity and suggest a mechanism independent of bulk cholesterol accumulation, pointing toward a mitochondrial mechanism underlying CYP-mediated neuroprotection.

supplemented_raw_records.title: The Gata2 3′-distal region is essential for IL-3 responsiveness in basophil and mast cell progenitors
supplemented_raw_records.abstract: The transcription factor GATA2 is highly expressed in mast cells and basophils and plays an important role in their development. We identified the Gata2 distal mast cell and basophil enhancer (G2DMBE), located 53 kb downstream of the murine Gata2 gene. G2DMBE is highly acetylated and bound by GATA2 in mast cells and basophils and is partially conserved in the human genome. G2DMBE deletion impaired interleukin-3 (IL-3)-dependent mast cell differentiation and basophil expansion. GATA2 expression increased at the mast cell and basophil progenitor stage, and this upregulation was attenuated by G2DMBE deletion. Consistently, expression of the IL-3 receptor β-chain genes Csf2rb and Csf2rb2 was also reduced in G2DMBE-deficient cells. These findings identify G2DMBE as a regulator of GATA2-dependent IL-3 responsiveness at the progenitor stage and provide a mechanism for sustaining lineage-specific transcriptional programs during mast cell and basophil development.

supplemented_raw_records.title: Epidemic waves and cytokine signatures of seven respiratory pathogens after COVID-19 restrictions
supplemented_raw_records.abstract: Non-pharmaceutical interventions (NPIs) during COVID-19 reduced population exposure to respiratory pathogens, creating population-level immunity debt. After these measures were lifted in China in May 2023, acute respiratory infections resurged with altered age distributions and co-infection dynamics. We conducted 20-month surveillance of 54,902 febrile patients and measured 47 plasma analytes in a nested cohort ( n = 187). Three sequential epidemic waves emerged: SARS-CoV-2 (July–August 2024), influenza A virus (IAV; December 2024–March 2025), and IAV plus human rhinovirus (November 2025–January 2026), with a 9.5% co-infection rate. G-CSF and IL-1Ra were elevated across all pathogens and tracked with clinical severity, whereas IAV-associated IL-4 elevation was severity-independent. A five-cytokine random forest classifier discriminated pathogen groups with 87.3% cross-validated accuracy. Pathogen-characteristic cytokine profiles may support etiological inference from single plasma samples and inform precision-medicine approaches to respiratory infections, pending external validation.

supplemented_raw_records.title: X-ray based 3D histology provides new anatomical and clinical insights into the human cribriform plate region
supplemented_raw_records.abstract: Detailed knowledge of the cribriform plate (CP) microanatomy, a fragile nasal-cranial interface, is important for studying olfaction, preventing iatrogenic injury, and managing cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) leaks. However, its composite architecture and neurovascular contents are incompletely resolved by clinical imaging and classical 2D histology. Here, we used cryogenic contrast-enhanced microCT (cryo-CECT), a nondestructive X-ray-based 3D histology approach, to image two cadaveric CP-region specimens. Cryo-CECT enabled micrometer-scale visualization of bone, vessels, nerves, and olfactory structures, including reconstruction of the CP, partitioned olfactory foramina, and the ethmoidal slit and cribroethmoidal foramen. We reconstructed a subset of olfactory fila from the lamina propria across the CP toward the olfactory bulbs and delineated the anterior ethmoidal artery and nerve, including vascular branches traversing olfactory foramina. Finally, color-coded thickness maps revealed regional heterogeneity in these specimens, suggesting that micrometer-scale mapping may refine assumptions about structurally vulnerable areas and support larger-scale anatomical and surgical-risk studies.

supplemented_raw_records.title: Cellular morphology emerges from polygenic, distributed transcriptional variation
supplemented_raw_records.abstract: Height and disease risk are canonical polygenic traits, but whether an analogous architecture governs cellular phenotypes remains unclear. Here, we show that cellular morphology behaves as a polygenic systems phenotype by integrating cross-modal modeling, perturbation profiling, and human genetic variation. An adversarially aligned autoencoder trained on four perturbation datasets predicted morphology from gene expression and generalized without retraining to matched RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) and cell painting profiles from 100 genetically diverse induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC) donors. Seventeen morphological features were strongly predicted, particularly those capturing organelle distribution and cytoskeletal architecture. Predictive signal was broadly distributed across genes, with weak individual gene-morphology correlations. Independent CRISPR perturbations supported model-prioritized genes including TIAM1 , RAB31 , and ABCC5 , while genetic analyses identified variant-gene-morphology associations involving PDHX, SLC11A2 , and MAPKAPK5 . These findings extend polygenic models of complex traits to cellular architecture and provide a framework for interpreting cross-modal prediction in functional genomics.

supplemented_raw_records.title: Neutral pH plasma-activated water eliminates ESKAPE pathogens via reactive nitrogen species enabling surface sanitation and wound care
supplemented_raw_records.abstract: Plasma-activated water (PAW) is an emerging antimicrobial strategy, although its efficacy has traditionally depended on acidic pH for reactive species generation. To improve clinical applicability, we developed a neutral-pH formulation using buffered water (hs-PAbW) and evaluated its antimicrobial activity and mechanism against ESKAPE pathogens. hs-PAbW significantly reduced bacterial viability during the exponential growth phase. While reactive oxygen species (ROS) alone were insufficient for bacterial killing, reactive nitrogen species (RNS), particularly peroxynitrite, mediated potent microbicidal effects through nitrotyrosine formation. These effects occurred independently of acidic conditions, demonstrating that antimicrobial activity is retained at neutral pH. hs-PAbW reduced bacterial burden on metal surfaces and exhibited greater in vitro killing than high concentrations of ceftazidime, ciprofloxacin, and meropenem. Furthermore, a noncytotoxic dose reduced bacterial load in infected wounds and accelerated wound closure in vivo . These findings highlight hs-PAbW as a sustainable, broad-spectrum antimicrobial agent with potential applications in surface sanitation and wound care.

supplemented_raw_records.title: Renal metabolic programming and glomerular morphological alterations in offspring of advanced maternal age mice
supplemented_raw_records.abstract: The developmental origins of health and disease (DOHaD) hypothesis proposes that the perinatal maternal environment influences disease susceptibility in adulthood. Advanced maternal age (AMA) is increasingly prevalent and associated with low birth weight (LBW) and cardiovascular risk. However, its impact on renal development in offspring remains unclear. Using an AMA mouse model, offspring kidneys were analyzed from birth to early adulthood by morphological, transcriptomic, and metabolomic profiling. AMA offspring displayed LBW, postnatal catch-up growth, and elevated blood pressure by eight weeks. Renal morphometry revealed reduced cortical glomerular density and increased glomerular tuft area. Bulk RNA-sequencing revealed coordinated downregulation of mitochondrial energy metabolism pathways. Metabolomic profiling identified exploratory signatures involving purine metabolism and acetyl-CoA-related metabolites. These findings suggest that maternal aging is associated with altered renal developmental and metabolic phenotypes in offspring. The relative contributions of prenatal AMA exposure and postnatal rearing by aged dams remain to be determined.

supplemented_raw_records.title: When one letter matters: Distinguishing VGF from VEGF in biomedical research
supplemented_raw_records.abstract: Scientific communication relies heavily on abbreviations to simplify complex terminology. When abbreviations are similar yet represent biologically distinct molecules; however, confusion can arise with consequences for literature interpretation, data retrieval, and scientific communication. One example is the recurring visual similarity between vascular growth factor (VGF; or proVGF), a neuroprotein precursor implicated in neuronal development, synaptic plasticity, metabolism, and neuropsychiatric disease, and vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF), a key regulator of angiogenesis and vascular function. Although these proteins belong to entirely different biological systems, their near-identical abbreviations create a structural risk of misreading among students, researchers, reviewers, and clinicians, a risk that may grow as literature search and screening increasingly rely on automated and AI-based tools. Here, we discuss the origins of this naming overlap, contrast the distinct biological roles of VGF and VEGF, and propose practical recommendations to reduce ambiguity in scientific communication.

supplemented_raw_records.title: Targeting SOST-LRRC15 axis impairs triple-negative breast cancer progression by regulating WNT signaling and EMT
supplemented_raw_records.abstract: Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) remains a therapeutic challenge due to its aggressive nature and lack of targeted therapies. Although sclerostin (SOST) is a well-established WNT regulator in bone metabolism, its role in cancer is poorly understood. Here, we identify SOST as a context-dependent oncogenic driver in TNBC. The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) analysis revealed  SOST  is highly upregulated in TNBC and correlates with poor survival. Functional studies demonstrated that SOST drives TNBC proliferation, migration, and invasion by activating WNT/β-catenin signaling and epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT). Using co-immunoprecipitation-mass spectrometry, we identified leucine-rich repeat-containing protein 15 (LRRC15) as a key SOST-binding partner facilitating its secretion, with co-expression predicting poor prognosis. We further uncovered that SOST function is regulated by P300-mediated acetylation at lysine 134 (K134). Therapeutic targeting of SOST using a specific aptamer or the small-molecule inhibitor SOSTi effectively suppressed TNBC malignancy. Our findings establish an SOST-LRRC15 axis promoting TNBC progression through WNT/EMT activation, positioning SOST as a promising therapeutic target.

supplemented_raw_records.title: Individual differences in sequential decision-making
supplemented_raw_records.abstract: People differ widely in how they make decisions in uncertain environments. While many studies leverage this variability to measure differences in specific cognitive processes and parameters, the key dimension(s) of individual variability in uncertain decision-making tasks has not been identified. Here, we analyzed behavioral data from 1,001 participants performing a restless three-armed bandit task, where reward probabilities fluctuated unpredictably over time. Using a novel analytical approach that controlled for the stochasticity in this task, we identified a dominant nonlinear axis of individual variability. We found that this primary axis of variability was strongly and selectively correlated with the probability of exploration, as inferred by latent state modeling. This suggests that the major factor shaping individual differences in bandit task performance is the tendency to explore (versus exploit), rather than reinforcement learning model parameters, personality characteristics, or low-level strategies. Certain demographic characteristics also predicted variance along this principal axis: participants at the exploratory end tended to be younger than participants at the exploitative end, and self-identified men were overrepresented at both extremes. Together, these findings offer a principled framework for understanding individual differences in task behavior while highlighting the cognitive and demographic factors that shape individual differences in decision-making under uncertainty.

supplemented_raw_records.title: TIPARP promotes M2-like macrophage polarization and associates with T2D myeloid alterations and PDAC progression
supplemented_raw_records.abstract: Type 2 diabetes (T2D) is associated with increased pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) risk, and diabetes-associated myeloid alterations may contribute to this relationship. We integrated single-cell analyses, Mendelian randomization (MR), and cellular and mouse models to investigate TIPARP-associated myeloid states. TIPARP expression was enriched in T2D classical monocytes, with predicted interactions involving macrophage-like monocytes. MR suggested a nominal association between genetically predicted higher TIPARP expression and PDAC risk (odds ratio [OR] = 2.15, p = 0.0044), with colocalization evidence (posterior probability of hypothesis 4 [PPH4] = 0.8023). TIPARP overexpression promoted M2-like polarization in THP-1-derived and primary human macrophages with PI3K-AKT involvement. Conditioned media from TIPARP-overexpressing macrophages enhanced PDAC cell proliferation and migration, while macrophage co-injection was associated with larger xenograft tumors. Matched blood and tumor samples showed associations between circulating TIPARP -positive ( TIPARP +) classical monocytes, intratumoral TIPARP + macrophages, and M2-like signatures. These findings suggest that TIPARP-associated myeloid alterations may represent a potential immunological link between T2D and PDAC progression.

supplemented_raw_records.title: Human visceral adipose NK cells associate with liver fibrosis-related indices and bariatric surgery weight loss
Enhanced phagocytosis and cytotoxicity of co-activated FcRγ-BAI1/FcRγ-MERTK dual-CAR monocytes drive potent anti-solid tumor activity
supplemented_raw_records.abstract: Chimeric antigen receptor macrophages (CAR-M) display superior tumor infiltration compared with CAR-T cells for solid tumor therapy, yet limited antitumor potency and antigen heterogeneity hinder their application. Direct engineering of chimeric antigen receptor monocytes (CAR-Mo) offers a simplified, cost-effective manufacturing alternative. Here, we engineered THP-1-derived monocytic cells with chimeric receptors containing FcRγ fused to phagocytosis-related cytoplasmic domains, targeting nucleolin and HER2. We constructed single-target and dual-antigen CAR-Mo platforms and evaluated their antitumor activity in vitro and in vivo . THP-1 monocytes carrying FcRγ-BAI1 or FcRγ-MERTK receptors exhibited enhanced phagocytosis, and dual-CAR-Mo achieved broader and stronger tumoricidal effects by targeting two tumor antigens. This dual-antigen-targeted CAR-Mo strategy activates both phagocytic and cytotoxic signaling pathways and represents a promising approach for solid tumor treatment. Collectively, this dual-target CAR-Mo strategy demonstrates promising antitumor efficacy in the THP-1 cell model, providing a feasible prototype for future optimization of solid tumor immunotherapy.

supplemented_raw_records.title: Bilateral V5 inhibition reduces asymmetric motion perception
supplemented_raw_records.abstract: Summary: Perceptual judgments can be systematically biased even when sensory evidence is balanced, yet the circuit mechanisms generating such asymmetries remain unclear. A notable example is the human tendency to report leftward more often than rightward motion. We tested whether this bias reflects unilateral hemispheric dominance or instead emerges from interhemispheric contributions of motion-sensitive areas. Participants performed a random-dot motion task at individually titrated coherence thresholds before and after inhibitory continuous theta-burst stimulation (cTBS) applied to left V5/MT+, right V5/MT+, or both sites. Unilateral perturbation left the bias unchanged, whereas only bilateral perturbation reduced it at the group-level, while sparing motion sensitivity. Trial-wise modeling converged on the same pattern. These results provide causal evidence that asymmetric motion perception is an emergent property of V5-V5 interactions rather than the output of a single dominant hemisphere. More broadly, these results highlight that interhemispheric interactions represent one of the mechanistic routes through which distributed sensory circuits shape perceptual bias.

supplemented_raw_records.title: Predicting local field potentials from spiking activity reveals state-dependent cortical dynamics
supplemented_raw_records.abstract: How local spiking activity gives rise to local field potentials (LFPs) across brain regions and states remains poorly understood. We combined multi-electrode recordings from the prefrontal and premotor cortex of two rhesus monkeys with a linear autoregressive model to predict LFPs from past multi-unit activity (MUA) during wakefulness, anesthesia, and recovery. We probed the spike-to-field mapping through LFP predictability. Under anesthesia, neural dynamics were characterized by structured, low-dimensional mappings. In contrast, wakefulness exhibited higher dimensionality and reduced predictability, indicating richer, more globally coordinated dynamics, whereas awakening showed intermediate, region-specific properties. Despite a breakdown of inter-area correlations during anesthesia, inter-area reconstructions remained robust and preserved LFP correlation structure, revealing large-scale constraints on cortical dynamics. The mapping pointed to state-dependent interactions between cortical areas and local adaptation-related processes. Despite its simplicity, the linear model captures key features of mesoscale organization and provides a link between local spiking activity and large-scale network dynamics.

supplemented_raw_records.title: Embryonic estrogens induce hypothalamic progesterone receptor expression to support brain feminization in birds
supplemented_raw_records.abstract: Embryonic estrogens are known to demasculinize the avian brain, but whether they actively promote brain feminization has remained unresolved. Here, transcriptomic analyses of the embryonic hypothalamus in Japanese quail identified progesterone receptor ( PGR ) as the principal estrogen-responsive gene showing female-biased expression.  PGR  expression required estrogen receptor activation and endogenous estrogen synthesis, and both progesterone and estrogens were detected in the female embryonic hypothalamus during the critical period of brain sexual differentiation. Embryonic treatment with the PGR antagonist PF-02413873 impaired adult egg laying without affecting male-typical sexual behavior. Together, these findings support a developmental hormonal cascade in which embryonic estrogens induce hypothalamic  PGR  expression, enabling progesterone signaling that may contribute to brain feminization in birds.

supplemented_raw_records.title: Mesoporous shell engineering of yolk-shell Fe3O4/carbon microspheres enables fast and durable sodium storage
supplemented_raw_records.abstract: Magnetite (Fe 3 O 4 ) is regarded as a high-capacity anode candidate for sodium-ion batteries; yet its practical application is largely impeded by severe volume fluctuations during conversion reactions and sluggish Na + transport kinetics. Here, we integrate a mesoporous carbon shell with an internal void in yolk-shell Fe 3 O 4 /carbon microspheres. This architecture combines conductive confinement and space for volume changes with accessible ion-transport pathways, enabling improved utilization of Fe 3 O 4 during repeated sodium storage. The electrode echibits a reversible capacity of 616.9 mAh g −1 at 0.05 A g −1 , with favorable rate performance; at 1 A g −1 , 90.2% of its capacity remains after 1,500 cycles. A pouch full cell paired with a Na 3 V 2 (PO 4 ) 3 -based cathode delivers 130.7 mAh, extending the evaluation beyond sodium-metal half-cells. These findings establish the performance benefits of mesoporous confinement within the Fe 3 O 4 system and support further assessment of this anode in sodium-ion batteries.

supplemented_raw_records.title: Enhancing bone defect repair by core-shell nanofibrous scaffolds through phase separation-activated autophagy process along with neurogenesis
supplemented_raw_records.abstract: Bone defects caused by aging or trauma often involve sensory loss, highlighting the need for scaffolds that support both bone regeneration and sensory recovery. This study reports an amino-modified mesoporous bioactive glass (MBG-NH 2 )/K63@silk fibroin (SF)/nerve growth factor (NGF) nanofiber scaffold. The scaffold showed nanoscale porosity, favorable mechanical properties, and calcium deposition in R-simulated body fluid (R-SBF). It promoted osteogenic differentiation of bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs) through Erk1/2-Runx2 signaling and induced autophagy via K63/p62/LC3-mediated separation, accompanied by increased expression of osteogenesis- and neurogenesis-specific genes. The scaffold supported neural differentiation, as indicated by increased expression of neurogenesis-related genes. The MBG-NH 2 /K63@SF/NGF scaffold significantly improved skull bone repair and the formation of new neurons within Haversian canals in the defect area of mice. The MBG-NH 2 /K63@SF/NGF scaffold promotes autophagy through phase separation and facilitates bone regeneration and neuron formation, indicating its potential as a multifunctional biomaterial for bone defect repair with neuron formation.

supplemented_raw_records.title: Evolutionary optimization of allosteric activation by Cl− and Cl− conduction in vesicular glutamate transporters
supplemented_raw_records.abstract: Vesicular glutamate transporters (VGLUTs) harness proton gradients to load glutamate into synaptic vesicles while mediating luminal chloride efflux through a channel-like conductance. We combined heterologous expression in mammalian cells, whole-cell patch-clamp recordings, and mathematical modeling to characterize the Drosophila melanogaster vesicular glutamate transporter DVGLUT and compare it with a rat counterpart, rVGLUT1. Like mammalian VGLUTs, DVGLUT couples glutamate transport to proton exchange at a 1:1 stoichiometry. In both transporters, luminal Cl − acts as a necessary allosteric activator, but DVGLUT displays higher apparent allosteric affinity than the rat transporter. DVGLUT anion channels exhibit lower unitary currents but higher open probabilities relative to rVGLUT1, resulting in larger Cl − currents in the presence of cytoplasmic glutamate. These differences between fly and mammalian transporters may reflect evolutionary adaptations to lower ion concentrations in Drosophila and underscore the importance of VGLUT allosteric regulation and anion channel activity in synaptic vesicle filling.

supplemented_raw_records.title: Synergistic delivery of FSTL1 and CHIR99021 in 3D bioprinted patches promotes adult mammalian heart repair
supplemented_raw_records.abstract: Recent advances in tissue engineering have positioned cardiac patch devices as a promising strategy to restore heart function and structure following myocardial infarction (MI). However, many existing patches are limited by the absence of vascular networks and insufficient biomolecular signals to effectively promote cardiomyocyte (CM) regeneration. In this study, we address these limitations by incorporating follistatin-like 1 (FSTL1) and CHIR99021 (CHIR) into a 3D bioprinted vascularized cardiac patch. The pro-proliferative effects of FSTL1 and CHIR on human induced pluripotent stem cell (hiPSC)-derived CMs were validated in vitro using 2D cultures, 3D hydrogel casts, and 3D bioprinted constructs. The synergistic impact of FSTL1 and CHIR was further evaluated in a rat model of acute MI. Treatment with the CHIR+FSTL1-loaded cardiac patch led to significant improvement in cardiac function and reduced fibrosis. Enhanced angiogenesis and increased CM proliferation were also observed following patch treatment. By integrating 3D bioprinting with targeted regenerative cues, this engineered cardiac patch presents strong therapeutic potential for myocardial repair.

supplemented_raw_records.title: ACTN4 promotes invasive phenotypes and WNT/β-catenin signaling through HDAC7-DACT2 regulation in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma
supplemented_raw_records.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) exhibits invasive growth and resistance to gemcitabine. We investigated how the actin-binding protein ACTN4 connects invasive behavior with WNT/β-catenin signaling. Elevated ACTN4 expression was associated with poorer survival in public PDAC cohorts and metastatic disease in genetically engineered mice. ACTN4 depletion reduced TGF-β1-induced invasion, focal adhesion signaling, and WNT activity, while increasing gemcitabine sensitivity in cells and organoids. Biochemical analyses and genetic rescue experiments linked Ser159-dependent ACTN4 activity to HDAC7 stability, reduced DACT2 expression, and β-catenin-dependent transcription. DACT2 depletion partially reversed the effects of ACTN4 loss. Ellagic acid reduced ACTN4-HDAC7 complex recovery and attenuated associated signaling. These findings support a functional model connecting ACTN4 to HDAC7-DACT2 regulation and identify an ACTN4-associated signaling axis relevant to PDAC invasion and gemcitabine response.

supplemented_raw_records.title: Feeder-free generation of lymphatic endothelial cells from human pluripotent stem cells
supplemented_raw_records.abstract: The lymphatic system plays an essential role in maintaining fluid homeostasis, lipid transport, and immune function. In this study, we developed a scalable, feeder-free method to differentiate human pluripotent stem cells (hPSCs) into lymphatic endothelial cells (LECs) that exhibit a predominantly fetal-like phenotype. By recapitulating key stages of lymphatic development, we first differentiated hPSCs into venous endothelial cells (VECs), which were subsequently directed toward a lymphatic endothelial fate. Using two independent hPSC lines, we demonstrated robust expression of lymphatic-specific markers and the capacity to form an endothelial network in vitro . We further characterized our differentiated populations through bulk RNA sequencing and compared their transcriptional profiles with pseudobulk data generated from human fetal and adult endothelial reference populations. These analyses revealed that hPSC-derived LECs preferentially associate with fetal LEC populations, supporting their developmental identity. This approach expands access to human LECs and provides a platform for investigating lymphatic development and disease.

supplemented_raw_records.title: S-palmitoylation regulates degradation of nuclear proteins in Schizosaccharomyces pombe
supplemented_raw_records.abstract: We have recently described a vital role of S-palmitoylation in regulating meiosis in Schizosaccharomyces pombe . In this study, we demonstrate that, to ensure proper meiosis, the protein levels of Erf2-Erf4 and Pfa3 palmitoyl acyltransferases are tightly regulated by meiotic gene transcription factors Mei4 and Atf21-Atf31, respectively. Intriguingly, the protein levels of Atf21 and Atf31 are regulated by another palmitoyl acyltransferase, Akr1, suggesting a functional two-way crosstalk between transcription and S-palmitoylation. In the absence of S-palmitoylation, Atf31 proteins are stabilized, forming nuclear foci resembling transcriptional condensates. We demonstrate that Cdc48 segregase interacts and extracts Atf31 together to be degraded by autophagy. In contrast, in the absence of S-palmitoylation, Atf21 proteins are targeted for proteasomal degradation. Thus, depending on the pathway, S-palmitoylation has different effects on the degradation of nuclear proteins. These results identify S-palmitoylation as an important modulator regulating selective degradation of nuclear proteins by the ubiquitin-proteasome or autophagy-lysosome proteolysis pathway.

supplemented_raw_records.title: Threat-induced behavioral plasticity in two invertebrate chordates integrates sensory and neuromodulatory inputs
supplemented_raw_records.abstract: Threat detection and evasion are fundamental challenges across the animal kingdom. Here, we examine threat detection and avoidance behaviors in two planktonic tunicates, Ciona intestinalis larvae and Oikopleura dioica adults, by quantifying locomotion and ecologically relevant behaviors in the presence of copepods. Both species exhibited marked increases in swimming speed, distance traveled, and roaming behavior upon predator exposure, whereas conditioned water alone had no effect. Despite this shared response, behavioral organization diverged: C. intestinalis primarily reallocated time toward roaming with few state transitions, while O. dioica increased behavioral switching, reduced dwelling, and prolonged roaming bouts. Pharmacological manipulations revealed species-specific effects of compounds targeting monoaminergic, glutamatergic, and GABAergic signaling: in C. intestinalis , bioamine, glutamatergic, and GABAergic perturbations disrupted threat-induced movement patterning, whereas in O. dioica they suppressed motility increases. Predator presence also accelerated metamorphosis and altered settlement in C. intestinalis , while in O. dioica it triggered rapid house escape, delayed expansion, and reduced turnover. Finally, we show that C. intestinalis larvae leverage a network of polymodal sensory neurons to detect chemical cues emanating from the copepods. Whole-brain calcium imaging suggested that these cues engage widespread yet structured neural activity across the larval brain, recruiting distributed neuronal populations with distinct temporal response motifs. Circuit-level analysis further indicated that sensory inputs propagate through a hierarchical sensorimotor network linking peripheral neurons to central interneurons and motor outputs, supporting a distributed transformation of threat-related information into behavior. These findings uncover conserved yet mechanistically distinct antipredator strategies in two evolutionarily distant tunicates.

supplemented_raw_records.title: Hippocampal CA1 neuronal ensembles efficiently discriminate routes during foraging- and homing-like task
supplemented_raw_records.abstract: In natural conditions, rodents continuously explore their environment and form spatial representations that enable them to navigate and locate relevant sites. Additionally, rodents rely on a route-based navigation strategy, consisting of well-defined paths that enhance efficiency and confer survival advantages. However, the contribution of the hippocampus to route-based navigation during continuous exploration—such as searching for resources and returning home—remains largely unexplored, particularly regarding its onset and the mechanisms of route discrimination. Here, we address this gap by investigating when and how hippocampal CA1 activity differentiates between overlapping trajectories in a continuously explored environment. Using calcium imaging in freely moving mice, we tracked neural activity as animals self-initiated routes in search of water. Our findings show that CA1 neurons rapidly establish an accurate global spatial map upon second exposure to the task. With increasing familiarity, route-specific representations progressively emerge and are maintained over the long term. In parallel with the refinement of these spatial representations, hippocampal involvement in route-choice prediction also develops with experience. Finally, our study provides insight into the neural basis of spatially flexible, ethologically relevant navigational strategies.

supplemented_raw_records.title: Visual-field position shapes input sampling and output routing in the superior colliculus
supplemented_raw_records.abstract: The location of visual stimuli influences the actions animals select, reflecting the distinct ecological and behavioral significance of the upper and lower visual fields. In mice, the superior colliculus transforms visual information into defensive and approach behaviors, with its superficial layers containing genetically defined cell types with distinct projections. Whether these circuits are repeated across visual space or are specialized by visual-field position remains unclear. Dual-color rabies tracing demonstrated that wide- and narrow-field neurons receive input from a largely shared set of brain regions, whereas upper- and lower-field domains sample these inputs differently. Some regions preferentially innervate one visual field domain; others contain spatially segregated neurons innervating each domain. Multiplexed analysis of projections by sequencing (MAPseq) showed that most superficial collicular neurons project to a single downstream target, but target probabilities differ between upper- and lower-field populations. Together, these findings identify visual-field position as a major organizing principle of input and output connectivity in the superficial superior colliculus.

supplemented_raw_records.title: Unlock the potential of power-to-ammonia in future multi-energy transition pathways
supplemented_raw_records.abstract: The high-renewable-energy transition toward a global carbon peak and neutrality represents a long-standing and formidable challenge. Although increasing attention has been paid to sector coupling and emerging energy carriers, how power-to-ammonia (P2A) may reshape spatiotemporal energy transitions amid technological and financial uncertainties has not been addressed. Here, we develop a risk-aware P2A-driven multi-energy transition pathway based on synergistic effects among electrical, ammonia, and thermal energy carriers. Taking Hubei Province and China as case studies across various technological and financial scenarios, we show that geographically spatiotemporal P2A and renewable energy development can reinforce each other, reducing conventional thermal generation by over 98.81% from 2030 to 2050 under high-renewable scenarios. We conclude that although the transition trajectory varies substantially with technological and financial risks, P2A-driven cross-sector multi-energy coupling can provide a promising pathway for accelerating energy system transition, particularly under the highly optimistic and exploratory P2A cost scenario of $100/kW.

supplemented_raw_records.title: CASCADE is an agentic AI framework for trustworthy biomarker discovery in precision oncology
supplemented_raw_records.abstract: Autonomous AI agents can now run end-to-end scientific analyses, yet no general method ensures those analyses are correct, and one upstream error can propagate across hundreds of downstream results at machine speed. We present CASCADE, an agentic validation framework built on mandatory, quantitatively gated analytical steps. Its central principle, specification-implementation separation, fixes what must be validated and to what standard while leaving how to the agent, so conclusions depend on the protocol rather than the model executing it. Every analysis is preserved as human-readable code with a complete decision log. Derived from a ∼25,000-patient clinical cancer genomics cohort and applied unmodified across three settings (13,424 patients), CASCADE recovered established signal, reported insufficient power instead of a false result where data were inadequate, and reversed a clinically consequential artifact (hazard ratio 0.84, corrected to 1.25). Findings were replicated in two independent multi-institutional cohorts, and three AI systems reproduced them with high fidelity.

supplemented_raw_records.title: Mulberrin regulates ferroptosis through the HIF-1α/STC2 axis to delay intervertebral disc degeneration induced by stress
supplemented_raw_records.abstract: Excessive mechanical loading contributes to intervertebral disc degeneration by disrupting extracellular matrix homeostasis and promoting ferroptosis. In this study, we investigated the protective effects of mulberrin using mechanically compressed nucleus pulposus cells (NPCs) and a rat-tail compression model. Mulberrin reduced ferroptosis-related injury, improved extracellular matrix metabolism, and attenuated stress-induced fibrosis, while alleviating disc degeneration in vivo . Transcriptomic and molecular analyses revealed increased expression of the anti-ferroptotic proteins SLC7A11 and GPX4 following mulberrin treatment. Further experiments showed that mulberrin increased hypoxia-inducible factor 1α (HIF-1α) expression and delayed its degradation, accompanied by enhanced transcription of stanniocalcin 2 (STC2). Gene knockdown experiments suggested that HIF-1α and STC2 contribute to these protective effects, although further validation is needed. These findings indicate that mulberrin may alleviate mechanically induced disc degeneration, at least partly through HIF-1α/STC2-associated regulation of ferroptosis.

supplemented_raw_records.title: Corrigendum/Erratum to “LCPBert: ProtBERT-based early-stage lung cancer prediction from T cell receptor beta sequences” [iScience 29 (2026) 15581]
Efficacy of second-line therapies for SMARCA4-mutated NSCLC based on a nationwide comprehensive genomic profiling database
supplemented_raw_records.abstract: Clinical data on existing therapies for SMARCA4 -mutated tumors are scarce, hindering the development of new agents targeting these mutations. Querying the Japanese C-CAT database, we analyzed non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) patients with oncogenic SMARCA4 mutations receiving docetaxel (DTX) alone or DTX plus ramucirumab (RAM) as second-line therapy following chemoimmunotherapy. The primary endpoint was the objective response rate (ORR). Among the 96,973 patients registered in C-CAT, 324 with oncogenic SMARCA4 -mutated NSCLC were identified. After first-line chemoimmunotherapy, 13 of these 324 patients received DTX alone and 52 received DTX+RAM. The ORR was 23.1% for DTX alone and 21.2% for DTX+RAM. Median time to next treatment was 4.0 months for DTX alone and 4.9 months for DTX+RAM. These findings clarify second-line DTX and DTX+RAM efficacy, establishing a benchmark for evaluating future therapies. Additionally, STK11 and KEAP1 co-mutations were characterized but showed no association with survival or second-line treatment outcomes.

supplemented_raw_records.title: Integrated fresh-frozen tissue and serum proteomics identifies pevonedistat response markers associated with progression-free survival
supplemented_raw_records.abstract: Summary: We evaluated the safety and tolerability of pevonedistat combined with capecitabine plus oxaliplatin in a phase I trial involving patients with unresectable advanced or recurrent gastric cancer. Serial endoscopic biopsy specimens collected before, during, and after treatment and matched serum extracellular vesicles (EVs) were analyzed using mass spectrometry-based proteomics, whereas serum proteins were profiled using proximity extension assay (PEA)-based proteomics to investigate pharmacoproteomic effects and explore blood-based biomarkers associated with tumor molecular signatures. In pre-treatment biopsies, 425 proteins correlated positively and 356 negatively with progression-free survival (PFS). Higher levels of KCNA3 and PITPNB in serum EVs and lower levels of CD5L, CD33, CALB2, SLC27A4, and NSFL1C in serum were associated with prolonged PFS. Collectively, our integrated proteomic analysis of biopsy tissues and blood identified tumor molecular signatures associated with treatment response and highlighted serum and serum EV proteomes as potential sources of minimally invasive biomarkers associated with clinical outcomes.

preserved_raw_outside_scope.title: Ancient Inuit dogs conform to a short-legged phenotype biomechanically advantageous for sledding
preserved_raw_outside_scope.abstract: Dog-powered transport is considered a key adaptation of Indigenous populations to Arctic life, but scarce bioarchaeological evidence makes it difficult to trace the origins and early spread of this practice. We hypothesized that selection for sledding might have favored certain skeletal traits over others and approached the question from a biomechanical perspective. We constructed a biomechanical model of forces acting on the dog skeleton during traction, showing that lowering the center of mass or shifting it forward is advantageous for traction. We therefore tested whether limb bones in modern and ancient sled dogs show relative shortening consistent with biomechanical expectation. Modern sled-dog groups, including Chukotka and Greenland dogs, differed from non-sled dogs and wolves by exhibiting a short-legged phenotype consistent with the biomechanical prediction. Archaeological samples of ancient Inuit dogs from Chukotka showed that most, including three ritually buried dogs, possessed the same phenotype as modern sled dogs.

preserved_raw_outside_scope.title: Developmental mechanism and evolutionary process of cephalopod suckers
preserved_raw_outside_scope.abstract: In contrast to animals possessing clear modularity such as vertebrates and arthropods, the evolution of novel structures in animals with indistinct body modules, like molluscs, remains poorly understood. Among molluscs, cephalopods have unique arms and suckers, which are particularly notable because they show clear modularity despite their derivation from a simple flat foot of the ancestral molluscs. However, their developmental mechanisms and evolutionary processes have yet to be revealed. Gene expression analyses of cephalopod arms and gastropod feet showed that well-known appendage patterning genes in animals with clear modularity were expressed in cephalopod arms and gastropod feet but not in suckers. Instead, genes such as Ets1 , typically involved in early embryonic processes like gastrulation in molluscs, were specifically expressed in suckers. These results suggest that cephalopod arms recruited developmental mechanisms similar to segmented appendages, whereas suckers represent a cephalopod-specific innovation formed through the co-option of genes contributing to early embryogenesis.

preserved_raw_outside_scope.title: Cross-species RNA sequencing identifies candidate lateralized genes in teleost brains
preserved_raw_outside_scope.abstract: Brain lateralization is widespread across vertebrates and contributes to hemispheric specialization. We compared left-right gene expression in the telencephalon and hindbrain of four phylogenetically distant teleosts: zebrafish, medaka, stickleback, and cichlid. Cross-species RNA sequencing identified five candidate genes with consistent directional expression biases. Although no genes remained significant after within-species FDR correction, Fisher's combined probability test supported directional asymmetry of five candidate genes. Notably, ddc and ntn1b were more highly expressed in the left hindbrain in three species and showed similar trends in the remaining species. GO analysis revealed shared functional categories associated with lateralized expression, including transport-related functions in the right-biased telencephalon and nervous system and developmental functions in the left-biased hindbrain. In situ HCR showed more ddc -expressing cells in the left median and dorsal raphe nuclei of medaka. These findings identify candidate molecular signatures associated with shared patterns of brain asymmetry across phylogenetically distant teleosts.

preserved_raw_outside_scope.title: A twentieth-century shift in psoriasis age at onset toward a metabolically associated phenotype
preserved_raw_outside_scope.abstract: Psoriasis, long regarded as a chronic immune-mediated skin disorder, is now recognized as a systemic inflammatory disease linked to metabolic dysfunction. Whether this link is intrinsic to the disease or a consequence of recent environmental change bears on how psoriasis is understood. We reconstructed the epidemiology of psoriasis from the early twentieth century onward, combining archival and citation-chain searches, logistic-growth modeling of historical prevalence, and Gaussian-mixture modeling of reconstructed age-at-onset data from pre- and post-World War II cohorts. Before the war, psoriasis arose in adolescents and young adults without metabolic comorbidity; over subsequent decades the age-at-onset distribution shifted toward older ages, and a middle-age-onset group associated with cardiometabolic disease became prominent, paralleling the population-wide rise of metabolic disease. We found no robust evidence that psoriasis itself became more frequent. These observational, hypothesis-generating findings are consistent with a shared environmental contribution to psoriasis and metabolic disease.

preserved_raw_outside_scope.title: Cats and humans show correlated affiliative physiological states
preserved_raw_outside_scope.abstract: Cats are among the world's most popular companion animals. Owner-pet hormonal synchrony is documented in dogs but untested in cats. We measured oxytocin and cortisol in 19 owners and 29 pet cats over one month, and examined owner mood and owner-cat proximity via Bluetooth beacons. Owner and cat oxytocin were positively associated, whereas their cortisol concentrations showed little association. Higher cat oxytocin was linked to lower owner cortisol and less negative mood, while higher owner cortisol was linked to more negative mood. Closer proximity predicted higher owner vigor, and exploratory behavioral testing linked cat oxytocin to social approach and cortisol to reduced approach toward strangers. Unlike the cortisol-centered synchrony reported in human-dog dyads, human-cat relationships may center on oxytocin, extending interspecies hormonal findings to a species with a distinct domestication history. These correlations may partly reflect shared household environments rather than dyad-specific interactions, an issue that future studies should address.

preserved_raw_outside_scope.title: An orthogonal Cro/OR3 system reveals an influence of astrocytes on motor neuron positioning
preserved_raw_outside_scope.abstract: Abstract Precise spatiotemporal control of gene expression is essential for dissecting complex biological systems. Here, we introduce a phage-derived Cro/O R 3 binary system for transcriptional activation that functions robustly in zebrafish and human cells. A Cro repressor fused to the VP16 activation domain efficiently drives expression of O R 3 operator-linked genes, and its activity can be targeted to specific cell types using enhancer-trap and promoter-controlled zebrafish lines. As a proof of concept, we manipulate glutamate transporter Glast/Slc1a3b-expressing cells in the central nervous system by Cro/O R 3-mediated expression of a human ataxia-associated, uptake-deficient Glast/Slc1a3b variant, causing spastic, uncoordinated movement and axial deformation. Concurrent Gal4/UAS-mediated visualization reveals substantially disrupted positioning of motor neurons, highlighting their selective sensitivity to extracellular glutamate homeostasis during spinal circuit assembly. Together, these results establish the Cro/O R 3 system as an orthogonal platform for targeted gene expression, enabling precise mechanistic dissection of how specific cell types and their interactions underlie diverse biological processes.

preserved_raw_outside_scope.title: Exploring viral diversity and functions in the deep-sea sediments of the Bay of Bengal: A first viromic account
preserved_raw_outside_scope.abstract: This study presents the viral communities in Bay of Bengal abyssal deep-sea sediment (3,747 m depth) characterized by employing metagenome based characterization. Illumina sequencing of virus-enriched sediment generated 39.4 million reads. A large proportion of these reads of ∼70% remained unclassified. The virome was dominated by dsDNA viruses, particularly Caudoviricetes , with Kyanoviridae as the most abundant family. As a result of assembly, 209 high-confidence viral contigs were recovered, and the gene-sharing network analysis revealed no clustering with known reference genomes, confirming predominantly uncharacterized viral lineages. Host predictions linked viruses to Pseudomonadota , Bacteroidota , and archaeal taxa including Nanoarchaeota . Functional annotation identified genes related to DNA replication and nucleotide metabolism, with limited auxiliary metabolic genes (AMGs) associated with carbohydrate and redox pathways. One complete circular ssDNA genome ( Genomoviridae ) was recovered. Overall, the Bay of Bengal deep-sea sediment harbors highly diverse, largely uncharacterized viral communities with potential roles in benthic biogeochemical cycling.

preserved_raw_outside_scope.title: CXCL12-CXCR4 signaling characterizes a targetable fibroblast-lymphocyte niche in pulmonary fibrosis
preserved_raw_outside_scope.abstract: Pulmonary fibrosis arises from diverse injuries but converges on progressive scarring without curative therapy. We integrated bulk and single-cell transcriptomic datasets from human idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF), silicosis, and non-IPF interstitial lung disease (ILD) and validated candidate pathways in human tissues and a silica-induced mouse model. CXCL12 and CXCR4 were recurrently upregulated in fibrotic lungs. CXCL12 localized mainly to fibroblast-lineage niches, while CXCR4-positive lymphocytes were consistently increased in fibrotic lungs. Cell-cell communication analysis and transwell assays supported a CXCR4-dependent lymphocyte migration toward conditioned medium from silica-stimulated fibroblasts. In human lung tissues, CXCR4-positive lymphocytes were associated with TGF-β-rich fibrotic regions. Therapeutic administration of Plerixafor after the establishment of fibrosis reduced lymphocyte accumulation, inflammatory cytokines, TGF-β-associated signaling, and extracellular matrix deposition in silica-exposed mice. These findings identify CXCL12-CXCR4 signaling as a targetable fibroblast-lymphocyte program in fibrotic lung disease.
